nodes.description: Nokia Fellow and Head of Radio Interface Group. Chairs the Next G Alliance Technology Roadmap Working Group (previously the National 6G Roadmap Working Group). Based at Nokia in Naperville, IL.

nodes.role: Former President, Bell Labs Core Research, Nokia (retired July 2026)
nodes.name: Peter Vetter
nodes.description: Led Bell Labs Core Research for nearly two decades, latterly as co-president of Bell Labs. Retired on 17 July 2026 when Nokia merged its two research units under new head Guru Parulkar, amid cuts and the move from Murray Hill to New Brunswick, NJ.

nodes.role: AT&T Fellow; AVP Wireless Technology & Standards, AT&T
nodes.name: Brian Daly
nodes.description: AT&T Fellow who leads AT&T's standards strategy. Co-chair of the FCC TAC 6G Working Group, co-chair of the Next G Alliance Steering Group, and co-lead of the National Spectrum Consortium 5G/Next G Working Group.

nodes.name: 3GPP
nodes.description: The global partnership that writes mobile standards (LTE, 5G NR and now 6G). Its plenaries include TSG RAN (radio) and TSG SA (system architecture). Support centre hosted by ETSI in Sophia Antipolis, France.

nodes.name: ITU-R Working Party 5D
nodes.description: The UN ITU group responsible for IMT standards, including IMT-2030 (6G). Sets the 6G requirements and evaluates candidate technologies such as 3GPP's.

nodes.name: ITU-APT Foundation of India (IAFI)
nodes.description: Non-profit Indian industry foundation and ITU sector member. Its President, Bharat Bhatia, chairs ITU-R WP 5D's Working Group on General Aspects for IMT-2030 (6G).

nodes.name: University of Surrey 6G Innovation Centre (6GIC)
nodes.description: The UK's first 6G Innovation Centre, within Surrey's Institute for Communication Systems (also home of the world's first 5G centre, 5GIC). Partners with InterDigital on 6G research and led the £12M government-funded TUDOR project.

nodes.name: Samsung R&D Institute UK
nodes.description: Samsung's UK research centre, part of Samsung's global 6G research program.

nodes.name: Ericsson UK 6G research program
nodes.description: Ericsson's UK-based 6G research program, launched in 2022 with a ten-year, tens-of-millions-of-pounds commitment and renewed in June 2025. Focus areas include multi-point transmission, integrated sensing and communication, cognitive networks, energy efficiency, resilience and security, feeding into 3GPP standards. Worked on the UK government-backed REASON and TUDOR projects.

nodes.name: TUDOR
nodes.description: Towards Ubiquitous 3D Open Resilient Network: a £12M DSIT-funded UK flagship 6G research project (Feb 2023 to Jan 2025) led by Surrey's 6GIC, integrating satellite, airborne and terrestrial networks. Consortium included Ericsson, InterDigital, BT, BAE Systems and Qualcomm.

nodes.address: Smart Internet Lab, University of Bristol
nodes.name: REASON
nodes.description: Realising Enabling Architectures and Solutions for Open Networks: UK 6G flagship project led by the University of Bristol (Professor Dimitra Simeonidou), with about £12m from DSIT (December 2022 to December 2025). Developed open 6G architectures and multi-technology access networks. Partners included Ericsson, Nokia Bell Labs, Samsung, BT, Digital Catapult, Thales UK, King's College London, Southampton and Strathclyde. Won the 2024 National AI Award for High Tech and Telecom.

nodes.name: University of Oulu / 6G Flagship
nodes.description: Finnish university running 6G Flagship, the world's first large-scale 6G research program (from 2018), directed by Ari Pouttu since 2025. Runs the 6G Test Centre, a NATO DIANA test centre, and leads the 6G Rocket AI-RAN project. Member of the AI-RAN Alliance.

nodes.name: Khalifa University 6G Research Center
nodes.description: 6G Research Center at Khalifa University, Abu Dhabi, founded in late 2023 and led by Merouane Debbah. Built TelecomGPT, a telco-first large language model, and works with GSMA Foundry on open telecom AI. Runs the KU–TII 6G Chair and co-hosts the 6G Abu Dhabi Summit with TII.

nodes.name: 6G Forum (Korea)
nodes.description: Korea's national 6G industry and research forum. Has run joint workshops with the Next G Alliance.

nodes.name: 6G Smart Networks and Services Industry Association (6G-IA)
nodes.description: European industry association for 6G; the private-side partner of the EU's Smart Networks and Services Joint Undertaking (SNS JU).

nodes.name: Bharat 6G Alliance
nodes.description: India's 6G alliance of industry, operators, academia and research institutions, launched by the Department of Telecommunications in July 2023. Grown to about 90 members with seven working groups. India targets at least 10% of global 6G patents and standards.

nodes.name: IMT-2030 (6G) Promotion Group (China)
nodes.description: China's government-backed 6G promotion group, set up by MIIT in June 2019 and led by CAICT. Coordinates research, standards, international cooperation and national 6G technical trials. Granted 6 GHz (6,425 to 7,125 MHz) trial spectrum by MIIT in May 2026.

nodes.name: XG Mobile Promotion Forum (XGMF)
nodes.description: Japan's forum promoting 5G evolution and 6G (Beyond 5G) research, standards and deployment.

nodes.name: NGMN Alliance
nodes.description: Global operator-led alliance (Next Generation Mobile Networks) that sets operator requirements and priorities for each generation, including 6G.

nodes.name: Huawei
nodes.description: Chinese telecoms vendor headquartered in Shenzhen and a major player in 6G research and standards. Participant in China's national 6G technical trials. Accounted for about 12% of China's 6G patent applications in a 2021 Nikkei survey.

nodes.role: Head of Cellular Standard, HWT Department, Apple
nodes.name: Wanshi Chen
nodes.description: Leads cellular standards at Apple. Formerly at Qualcomm (from 2006), where he was 3GPP TSG RAN Plenary Chair (April 2021 to January 2025, the most senior radio role in 3GPP), RAN1 Chair (2017 to 2021) and RAN1 Vice Chair (2013 to 2017), leading delivery of the first 5G NR releases. Lead Editor of IEEE Communications Magazine's Mobile Communications and Network Series.

nodes.role: Master (VP of Technology), Samsung Research; 3GPP TSG RAN Chair
nodes.name: Younsun Kim
nodes.description: Current 3GPP TSG RAN Chair (elected March 2025, term to March 2027) and the first Korean in the role. Samsung Research Master; previously chaired RAN WG1 (2021–2025). Succeeded Wanshi Chen.

nodes.role: Senior Principal Engineer & Senior Director of Standards, Intel; 3GPP TSG SA Chair
nodes.name: Puneet Jain
nodes.description: 3GPP TSG SA (Service and System Aspects) Plenary Chair since 2023, re-elected for a second term in March 2025. Previously chaired SA WG2.

nodes.role: Samsung Research; Chair, ITU-R Coordination Group on IMT-2030 (6G)
nodes.name: HyoungJin Choi
nodes.description: Samsung Research researcher named chair of ITU-R WP 5D's Coordination Group on IMT-2030 (6G) in July 2024, serving until 2029. Previously chaired the ITU-R 6G Vision Group (2021–2023).

nodes.role: President, IAFI; Chair, ITU-R WP 5D Working Group on General Aspects
nodes.name: Bharat Bhatia
nodes.description: President of the ITU-APT Foundation of India and Vice Chairman of the Wireless World Research Forum. Chairs ITU-R WP 5D's Working Group on General Aspects, which develops IMT-2030 (6G) documents including the call for candidate technologies.

nodes.role: Regius Professor; Founding Director, 5GIC, 6GIC and Institute for Communication Systems, University of Surrey
nodes.name: Rahim Tafazolli
nodes.description: Regius Professor of Electronic Engineering at Surrey and founder and director of the Institute for Communication Systems, the 5G Innovation Centre and the 6G Innovation Centre (the UK's first). Led the £12M TUDOR project and set up a 6G research partnership with InterDigital.

nodes.role: Vice Rector for Research, University of Oulu; former Director, 6G Flagship
nodes.name: Matti Latva-aho
nodes.description: Led Finland's 6G Flagship from its start in 2018 until mid-2025. Vice Rector for Research at the University of Oulu since July 2025 (term to 2030). IEEE Fellow.

nodes.name: Ari Pouttu
nodes.description: Director of 6G Flagship since 2025, succeeding Matti Latva-aho (previously Vice-Director).

nodes.role: Director of Sustainability and Regulation, 6G Flagship
nodes.name: Marja Matinmikko-Blue
nodes.description: Director of Sustainability and Regulation at 6G Flagship, University of Oulu; works on the path from 6G research to spectrum regulation.

nodes.name: Erik Dahlman
nodes.description: One of the most influential architects of the LTE and 5G standards, now leading Ericsson's 6G standardisation work with Stefan Parkvall. Keynote at the 6G@UT Forum 2025.

nodes.role: Senior Expert, Cellular Radio Access, Ericsson
nodes.name: Stefan Parkvall
nodes.description: One of the most influential architects of the LTE and 5G standards, now leading Ericsson's 6G standardisation work with Erik Dahlman. Keynote at the 6G@UT Forum 2025.

nodes.name: Merouane Debbah
nodes.description: Founding director of Khalifa University's 6G Research Center. Leads TelecomGPT, a telco-first large language model, and the GSMA Foundry collaboration on open telecom AI. A key name where AI and 6G meet.

nodes.role: Senior Vice President, 6G Research Team, Samsung; Vice Chair, Next G Alliance Full Member Group
nodes.name: Charlie Zhang
nodes.description: SVP at Samsung Research America and head of Samsung Research's 6G team, which publishes Samsung's 6G white papers. Vice Chair of the Next G Alliance Full Member Group. Former 3GPP RAN WG1 vice chair. IEEE Fellow. Quoted as Samsung Executive Vice President on the July 2026 Verizon ISAC trial in Dallas.

nodes.role: EVP and Head, Advanced Communications Research Center (ACRC), Samsung Research
nodes.name: JinGuk Jeong
nodes.description: Heads Samsung Research's Advanced Communications Research Center, leading research on AI-native networks and ISAC. Signed 6G MOUs with SK Telecom (AI-RAN, 2025) and LG Uplus (ISAC, 2026), and leads partnerships such as the Verizon 6G Innovation Forum.

nodes.role: Founding Chair, Bharat 6G Alliance; Chairman, Tejas Networks
nodes.name: N. G. Subramaniam
nodes.description: Founding chair of the Bharat 6G Alliance. Chairman of Tejas Networks and former COO of TCS.

nodes.name: Younghan Nam
nodes.role: Senior Director, Standards and Mobility Innovation Team, Samsung Research America
nodes.description: Senior Director in Samsung Research America's Standards and Mobility Innovation Team, where he leads 6G cellular system research. Earlier led 3GPP RAN1 work on mmWave, massive MIMO and 5G channel modelling. Works in Charlie Zhang's team. Speaker at the Next G Alliance and 6G Forum Korea joint workshop.

nodes.name: Vodafone Group
nodes.description: Global mobile operator. Its Group R&D team, led by Luke Ibbetson, shapes Vodafone's thinking on 6G, non-terrestrial networks and quantum. Separate from VodafoneThree, its UK joint venture.

nodes.name: Luke Ibbetson
nodes.role: Head of Group R&D, Vodafone Group; Board Director, NGMN
nodes.description: Head of Group R&D at Vodafone, with the company since 1996. Shapes Vodafone's thinking on 6G, non-terrestrial networks and quantum; pioneer of NB-IoT. Board director of the NGMN Alliance. Argues operators should deploy 6G when the technology is mature and in step with network refresh cycles. Named on the UK REASON project.

nodes.name: Christian Fager
nodes.role: Professor of Microwave Electronics, Chalmers University of Technology
nodes.description: Professor of Microwave Electronics at Chalmers and a project leader on the three-year Chalmers–Virginia Tech project on energy-efficient 6G radio, funded by the Swedish Research Council and NSF (VINES). Works on moving signal processing from the radio into the fibre network to cut energy losses.

nodes.name: Lars Svensson
nodes.role: Associate Professor of VLSI Systems, Chalmers University of Technology
nodes.description: Associate Professor of VLSI Systems at Chalmers, on the three-year Chalmers–Virginia Tech project on energy-efficient 6G radio funded by the Swedish Research Council and NSF (VINES).

nodes.name: Virginia Diodes (VDI)
nodes.address: 979 Second Street SE, Suite 309, Charlottesville, VA 22902
nodes.description: Makes millimetre-wave and terahertz test and measurement equipment and components (50 GHz to 2 THz), including network analyser, spectrum analyser and signal generator extension modules, built on in-house GaAs Schottky diodes. Relevant to sub-THz 6G research. Founded in 1996 as a University of Virginia spin-off; about 100 staff.

nodes.name: Thomas W. Crowe
nodes.description: CEO and founder of Virginia Diodes, the Charlottesville terahertz component and test equipment maker spun out of the University of Virginia in 1996.

nodes.name: Gerhard Schoenthal
nodes.description: Chief Operating Officer of Virginia Diodes, with the company since 2004. Speaks on terahertz technology for 6G, including at the 2020 6G Symposium. Physics PhD from the University of Virginia; former US Navy officer and Intel process engineer.

nodes.name: Nishith D. Tripathi
nodes.role: Research Associate Professor, ECE, Virginia Tech
nodes.description: Research associate professor in electrical and computer engineering at Virginia Tech. Principal investigator, with Jeff Reed as co-PI, on 'Securing Non-Terrestrial Networks in NextG', a 2021 Commonwealth Cyber Initiative project on security risks in satellite and air-to-ground networks for 6G.

nodes.name: ANSER (Analytic Services Inc.)
nodes.description: Not-for-profit public-service research institute supporting national and homeland security through independent analysis and practical solutions. Founded in 1958 as an Air Force federal contract research centre. Has a wireless communications policy practice covering 5G, ISAC, Open RAN, AI-RAN, spectrum management and satellite networking.

nodes.name: Department of War Office of the CIO
nodes.description: Office of the Department of War (Defense Department) Chief Information Officer, principal adviser to the Secretary of War on IT, cybersecurity, communications and spectrum. Leads the DoW 5G/6G enterprise strategy and 5G reference architecture for military installations; oversees DISA.

nodes.role: Chief Information Officer, Department of War
nodes.name: Kirsten Davies
nodes.description: Department of War CIO, sworn in on 23 December 2025 after Senate confirmation. Principal adviser to the Secretary of War on IT, cybersecurity and information assurance; oversees DISA. Her office runs the DoW 5G/6G enterprise strategy. Previously CISO at Unilever.

nodes.name: Ofinno
nodes.description: Research and development lab that invents and patents wireless and video technologies for 5G/6G, next-gen Wi-Fi (IEEE 802.11) and video compression standards. Its 6G work sits in a dedicated 6G Innovation Lab in Reston, with 3GPP delegates mainly in RAN1 and RAN2. Founded in 2011 by Esmael Dinan. Named a LexisNexis Top 100 Global Innovator for the fifth year running in 2026.

nodes.name: Kavon Nasabzadeh
nodes.description: CEO of Ofinno, the Reston R&D and patent lab working on 5G/6G, next-gen Wi-Fi and media compression standards.

nodes.name: Ali Cagatay Cirik
nodes.role: Technical Director, Senior Principal Engineer, Ofinno
nodes.description: Technical Director for 5G and 6G at Ofinno's 6G Innovation Lab in Reston, at Ofinno since 2017. Works on 5G NR and MIMO signal processing. Previously at Sierra Wireless and a research fellow at the University of Oulu, Edinburgh and UBC. PhD, UC Riverside.

nodes.name: Taehun Kim
nodes.role: Senior Research Manager, Principal Engineer, Ofinno
nodes.description: Leads research on 5G and 6G radio access network procedures at Ofinno. Formerly chief research engineer for standardisation at LG Electronics, a 3GPP CT1 and RAN2 delegate, and rapporteur for a V2X work item. PhD, KAIST; postdoc at UCLA.

nodes.name: Yunjung Yi
nodes.role: Senior Manager, Senior Principal Engineer, Ofinno
nodes.description: Researches radio access technologies for LTE, NR and 6G at Ofinno. 3GPP delegate since 2011, working on LTE MTC, NB-IoT, 5G control channel and initial access, URLLC, SBFD and power saving. PhD, UCLA.

nodes.name: HyoungSuk Jeon
nodes.role: Senior Manager, Senior Principal Engineer, Ofinno
nodes.description: Senior Manager and Senior Principal Engineer in Ofinno's 6G Innovation Lab, Reston.

nodes.name: Sechang Myung
nodes.description: 3GPP RAN1 researcher in Ofinno's 6G Innovation Lab, working on network energy saving, initial access, and high-frequency and unlicensed spectrum.

nodes.name: Chiou-Wei (Joanne) Tsai
nodes.description: 3GPP RAN1 delegate and inventor in Ofinno's 6G Innovation Lab, working on 6G control channel design, scheduling and HARQ. RAN1 delegate since 2017; Feature Lead for Rel-20 6GR Bandwidth Operation. Formerly at MediaTek.

nodes.name: Umut Ugurlu
nodes.description: 3GPP delegate at Ofinno working on MIMO, beam management, HARQ, initial access, and integrated sensing and communications (ISAC).

nodes.name: Javad Abdoli
nodes.description: Inventor at Ofinno focused on the 6G air interface. Formerly a 3GPP RAN1 delegate at Huawei and Intel, and a systems engineer at Mavenir and Samsung Research America. Named on 45+ US patents. PhD, University of Waterloo.

nodes.name: Jae-Nam Shim
nodes.description: 3GPP RAN1 delegate at Ofinno working on 5G/6G wireless communications. Formerly in the standards division at LG Electronics.

nodes.name: Hyunsu Cha
nodes.description: Research engineer at Ofinno working on 6G initial access, MIMO, positioning, ISAC, Ambient IoT and AI/ML for wireless. 3GPP RAN1 delegate since 2017. Formerly senior staff engineer for 5G/6G research at Nokia Standards. PhD, Yonsei University.

nodes.name: Govind Ravikumar Gopal
nodes.description: Works on AI/ML for 5G/6G channel state information (CSI) in 3GPP RAN1 at Ofinno. Formerly led 6G radio research in Nokia's Technology Standards group.

nodes.name: Jaehoon Chung
nodes.description: 3GPP RAN1 standards engineer at Ofinno working on AI/ML-based CSI compression, beam management and MIMO.

nodes.name: Bighnaraj Panigrahi
nodes.description: 5G-Advanced and 6G research and standardisation at Ofinno (3GPP RAN2). Formerly at Nokia and TCS.

nodes.name: Heng-Li (Henry) Chin
nodes.description: Layer 2 protocol specialist and inventor at Ofinno (3GPP RAN2), with 90+ patents. Formerly at MediaTek.

nodes.name: Joondoo Kim
nodes.description: 6G standards research engineer at Ofinno focused on 3GPP RAN2 user plane. Spent 14 years at Samsung Electronics as a network system architect on MAC scheduling for 4G/5G base stations. PhD, Yonsei University.

nodes.name: GyeongCheol Lee
nodes.description: Specialist in 3GPP RAN2 user plane protocols at Ofinno, with 10+ years on LTE, NR and 6G. Formerly RAN2 UP Manager at LG Electronics.

nodes.name: Marta Martinez Tarradell
nodes.description: 3GPP RAN2 delegate at Ofinno working on 4G/5G/6G wireless standardisation.

nodes.name: Jaewook Lee
nodes.description: 3GPP RAN2 contributor at Ofinno, in RAN2 since 2009. Previously worked on LTE and NR standards at LG Electronics and on network systemisation at Ericsson LG.

nodes.name: Tiep Hoang
nodes.description: Patent engineer at Ofinno with a research background in physical layer security, reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) and AI/ML optimisation for wireless. Postdoc at RIT, CU Denver and Southampton. PhD, Queen's University Belfast.

nodes.name: Aloizio P. Da Silva
nodes.description: Director of the CCI xG Testbed in Arlington since 2020, leading a team of faculty, postdocs, graduate research assistants and interns. Works on wireless networking (NFV, SDN, SDR), radio access and core networks, and large-scale testbed experimentation. Also research faculty in Virginia Tech's Bradley Department of ECE. Previously with the NSF PAWR program. Not related to CCI executive director Luiz DaSilva.

nodes.name: Joao Santos
nodes.role: Research Assistant Professor; 5G Testbed and AI Assurance Researcher, CCI
nodes.description: CCI research assistant professor working on radio resource management, radio virtualisation, network slicing, network security and end-to-end orchestration. PI on an NSF CISE CORE grant (about $553k, three years) on natively resilient 6G networks.

nodes.name: Sayanta Seth
nodes.description: Postdoctoral associate on the CCI xG Testbed working on O-RAN, digital twins, AI-native wireless, FR3/mmWave spectrum coexistence, 6G and cislunar communications, plus commercial O-RAN interoperability and security testing. Formerly a postdoc at NC State's NextG Wireless Lab. PhD, University of Central Florida.

nodes.name: WiSig Networks
nodes.address: Academic Block-C, IIT Hyderabad, Kandi, Sangareddy, Telangana 502285, India
nodes.description: Indian 5G and O-RAN equipment, software and services company (O-CU, O-DU, O-RU, SMO, massive MIMO radios), incubated at IIT Hyderabad and founded in 2016 by Prof Kiran Kuchi. Testing its O-RAN components at the CCI xG Testbed OTIC for global commercialisation.

nodes.name: DISH Wireless (EchoStar)
nodes.description: EchoStar subsidiary that built the first US standalone Open RAN 5G network and co-hosted the North American O-RAN OTIC at CCI. After EchoStar sold spectrum to AT&T and SpaceX in 2025, Dish began decommissioning its Open RAN network; Dish Wireless filed for bankruptcy in 2026. Ran the NTIA-funded ORCID Open RAN test centre in Cheyenne, WY.

nodes.name: Jacek Kibilda
nodes.role: Research Associate Professor, CCI and Virginia Tech ECE
nodes.description: Research associate professor at CCI and Virginia Tech's Bradley Department of ECE, and associate research faculty on the xG Testbed. Models and designs NextG mobile networks using stochastic geometry, AI and optimisation. Formerly a research fellow at CONNECT, Trinity College Dublin.

nodes.name: Madhura Adeppady
nodes.description: Postdoctoral researcher on the CCI xG Testbed working on resource-efficient orchestration of microservices in edge computing, interference-aware placement and serverless systems.

nodes.name: Zeeshan Shah
nodes.role: Principal Engineer, Verizon 5G O-RAN Lab; resident engineer at CCI xG Testbed
nodes.description: Verizon principal engineer based at the CCI xG Testbed as a resident engineer, working on 5G O-RAN ACCoRD testing and integration.

nodes.name: Md. Habibur Rahman
nodes.role: PhD student and graduate research assistant, CCI xG Testbed
nodes.description: Virginia Tech electrical engineering PhD student and CCI graduate research assistant on the xG Testbed, working on machine learning for wireless networks and O-RAN.

nodes.name: Asheesh Tripathi
nodes.role: PhD student and graduate research assistant, CCI xG Testbed
nodes.description: Virginia Tech PhD student and CCI graduate research assistant working on spectrum sharing, ML in wireless systems, O-RAN and the SDR-based CBRS testbed at Stroubles Creek. Co-author of the testbed's 2025 IEEE Communications Magazine paper.

nodes.name: Mahesha Vidurange
nodes.description: Doctoral student on the CCI xG Testbed working on O-RAN security and interoperability and AI/ML-based management.

nodes.name: Ishtiaque Ahmed
nodes.description: Doctoral student on the CCI xG Testbed working on cloud solutions for O-RAN and ACCoRD interoperability testing.

nodes.name: Manikantha Rayudu
nodes.description: Doctoral student on the CCI xG Testbed working on federated learning for IoT, extending to O-RAN.

nodes.name: Atif Ahmed
nodes.description: Research intern on the CCI xG Testbed working on O-RAN Open Fronthaul testing for ACCoRD.

nodes.name: Harshit Sai Teja Doddi
nodes.role: Master's Researcher / Intern, CCI xG Testbed
nodes.description: Master's researcher and intern on the CCI xG Testbed admin team, handling network administration and management.

nodes.name: Kiran Kuchi
nodes.role: Founder, WiSig Networks; Professor, IIT Hyderabad
nodes.description: Founder of WiSig Networks and professor of electrical engineering at IIT Hyderabad. Contributor to 3GPP 5G/6G standards and works with the Indian government on its 6G roadmap. Leading WiSig's O-RAN testing with the CCI xG Testbed.

nodes.name: Abside Networks
nodes.description: US designer and manufacturer of 4G/5G and O-RAN radio systems, including massive MIMO units and private 5G SA systems for federal spectrum (n79). xG Testbed partner at CCI and a RAPID ISAC awardee with Northeastern University.

nodes.name: Altio Labs
nodes.description: R&D firm adapting 3GPP cellular technology for DoD uses: telemetry, positioning and sensing. RAPID ISAC awardee with Arizona State, DASH Tech IC and Mississippi State.

nodes.name: Arizona State University
nodes.description: Public research university. RAPID ISAC team member with Altio Labs, DASH Tech IC and Mississippi State.

nodes.name: DASH Tech Integrated Circuits
nodes.description: SoC design firm spun out of Arizona State and the University of Michigan in 2021. Builds domain-adaptive processors for RF sensing and communications at the edge, for commercial and DoD use. RAPID ISAC team member.

nodes.name: Mississippi State University
nodes.description: Public research university. On two RAPID ISAC teams: with Altio Labs, ASU and DASH Tech IC, and on the INSPIRED ISAC platform with NC State and the University of Utah.

nodes.name: Michigan State University
nodes.description: Public research university. RAPID ISAC awardee with George Mason University; also leads an NTIA-funded AI-driven O-RAN testing project with GMU.

nodes.name: Leidos
nodes.description: Defence, IT and science integrator. RAPID ISAC awardee with Tiami Networks.

nodes.name: University of Utah
nodes.description: Public research university and home of the POWDER PAWR wireless testbed. On the RAPID INSPIRED ISAC platform team ($3M) with NC State and Mississippi State.

nodes.name: System & Technology Research (STR)
nodes.description: Defence R&D company. RAPID ISAC awardee with Northeastern University.

nodes.name: Texas A&M University
nodes.description: Public research university. RAPID ISAC team member with UC San Diego, IBM and Northrop Grumman. Academic partner on the CCI xG Testbed project.

nodes.name: IBM
nodes.description: Technology company. RAPID ISAC team member with Texas A&M, UC San Diego and Northrop Grumman.

nodes.name: ANDRO Computational Solutions
nodes.description: Defence and commercial R&D firm working on software-defined waveforms, AI for RF spectrum sensing and wireless networking. RAPID ISAC team member with Parallel Wireless and Virginia Tech.

nodes.name: Salvador D'Itri
nodes.role: Chairman, National Spectrum Consortium; Co-Founder, Federal AI Accelerator
nodes.description: Chair of the National Spectrum Consortium, which oversees a 350+ member ecosystem and the OTA contracting vehicle for DoW next-generation wireless prototypes. Co-founder of the Federal AI Accelerator, a Carahsoft event series. Long-time Federated Wireless executive (VP Federal) and former Wireless Innovation Forum board member. Previously chaired NSC 2019 to 2021. Speaker at FedInsider's NextGen Cellular Networks event.

nodes.name: David Kirkwood
nodes.role: Program Manager, OCUDU, FutureG Office, OUSW(R&E)
nodes.description: Program Manager for the FutureG Office's OCUDU program. Building the public-private partnership behind OCUDU with the Linux Foundation and the National Spectrum Consortium, including the OCUDU Ecosystem Foundation (68+ members).

nodes.name: Deutsche Telekom
nodes.description: German telecoms group and majority owner of T-Mobile US. Its Group Technology unit runs network strategy, architecture, standardisation and patents, and is steering the group towards AI-native networks and 6G. Long-standing NGMN Alliance board member.

nodes.name: Arash Ashouriha
nodes.description: Leads Group Technology at Deutsche Telekom: technology strategy, network evolution, architecture, standardisation, patents and innovation, including the move to AI-native networks and 6G. Previously headed Group Technology Architecture & Innovation, steering DT's 5G work. Chaired the NGMN Alliance Board 2020 to 2025. Joined DT in 2016 after 15 years at Vodafone Group, latterly Chief Network Officer for Germany & Central Europe.

nodes.name: Networks and Systems Security Lab (NSSL), Virginia Tech
nodes.description: Virginia Tech security lab led by Professors Angelos Stavrou and Haining Wang. Work spans NextG and 5G/6G security, cellular and wireless network security, Zero Trust and Named Data Networking for 6G, post-quantum cryptography for 5G, and AI security.

nodes.name: Quokka (formerly Kryptowire)
nodes.address: 3031 Tisch Way, Suite 505, San Jose, CA 95128
nodes.description: Mobile app and firmware security company founded in 2011 as Kryptowire by Angelos Stavrou, then at George Mason University, with DARPA and DHS funding. Products: Q-mast, Q-scout and Q-firm (Android firmware analysis for telcos and device makers, launched March 2026).

nodes.name: Wireless Infrastructure Association (WIA)
nodes.description: Trade association for the businesses that build, develop, own and operate US wireless infrastructure. Advocates for widespread deployment of wireless infrastructure to enable connectivity everywhere.

nodes.name: University of Texas at Arlington (UTA)
nodes.description: Public research university. Home of the Transformative Wireless Systems and Technology (TWiST) Lab in the Computer Science and Engineering department, working on ML for wireless, O-RAN, ISAC and wireless digital twins for 6G.

nodes.name: Angelos Stavrou
nodes.role: Professor, ECE, Virginia Tech; Founding Professor, VT Institute for Advanced Computing
nodes.description: Professor in Virginia Tech's Bradley Department of ECE and founding professor and entrepreneurship lead at the VT Institute for Advanced Computing in Alexandria. Co-leads the Networks and Systems Security Lab, working on security and localisation for NextG and mobile devices. Founder and Chief Science Officer of Quokka (formerly Kryptowire). Former George Mason University professor. PI on NSF, DARPA, IARPA, DHS and DoD research awards.

nodes.name: Haining Wang
nodes.role: Professor, ECE, Virginia Tech; IEEE Fellow
nodes.description: Professor in Virginia Tech's Bradley Department of ECE and co-lead of the Networks and Systems Security Lab. IEEE Fellow (2020) for contributions to network and cloud security. Works on cybersecurity, networking systems, cloud and cyber-physical systems. CCI researcher. Previously professor at the University of Delaware.

nodes.name: Pragya Sharma
nodes.description: PhD candidate advised by Angelos Stavrou and Haining Wang, working on cellular and wireless network security and machine learning in wireless environments.

nodes.name: Kene Nwodo

nodes.description: Signed a three-year research MoU with Ericsson (February 2024) for a joint centre on sustainable and trustworthy cyber-physical systems for the AI and 6G era.

nodes.name: DoT (India Department of Telecommunications)
nodes.description: India's telecoms department. Launched the Bharat 6G Alliance (July 2023), funds 6G testbeds through the Telecom Technology Development Fund (Digital Bharat Nidhi) and published India's Spectrum Roadmap for 6G.

nodes.name: C-DOT (Centre for Development of Telematics)
nodes.address: C-DOT Campus, Mehrauli, New Delhi, India
nodes.description: India's government telecoms R&D centre. Built India's indigenous 4G core and is being pushed to lead national 6G, AI, quantum and cybersecurity work. Set up a Centre of Excellence at IISc (2026).

nodes.name: TSDSI (Telecommunications Standards Development Society, India)
nodes.description: India's telecoms standards body and 3GPP organisational partner. Contributed to the ITU-R IMT-2030 framework; the Indian delegation added the Ubiquitous Connectivity usage scenario and the Coverage capability.

nodes.name: Capgemini 6G Research Lab (Gurugram)
nodes.description: Capgemini's 6G research lab, launched May 2023. Builds test beds and simulators for 6G use cases, AI algorithms for 6G wireless challenges and energy-saving solutions. Builds on Capgemini's 6G research with King's College London.

nodes.name: Bharti Airtel
nodes.description: Indian mobile operator. Working with Ericsson and Volvo on XR and digital twins at Volvo's Bengaluru R&D centre.

nodes.name: Reliance Jio
nodes.description: Indian mobile operator. Took part in DoT's 2026 technical discussion on AI-native 6G and quantum-secure networks.

nodes.name: Govindan Rangarajan
nodes.description: IISc Director who signed the 2024 6G research partnership with Nokia.

nodes.name: Nitin Bansal
nodes.description: Leads Ericsson India, including its India 6G program and Bengaluru ASIC expansion.

nodes.name: Radha Krishna Ganti
nodes.role: Faculty, Department of Electrical Engineering, IIT Madras
nodes.description: Lead IIT Madras investigator on the indigenous 5G testbed base station; IIT Madras team now works on 6G.

nodes.name: Sanghamitra Bandyopadhyay
nodes.description: ISI Director who backed the joint ISI-Ericsson research centre on cyber-physical systems for AI and 6G (2024).

nodes.name: Rajkumar Upadhyay
nodes.description: Leads C-DOT; signed its Centre of Excellence at IISc for 6G, AI, quantum and cybersecurity (2026).

nodes.name: Shamik Mishra
nodes.role: Chief Technology and Innovation Officer, Connected Futures, Capgemini
nodes.description: Launched Capgemini's 6G research lab in Gurugram (2023).

nodes.name: Rajavelsamy Rajadurai
nodes.role: Principal Architect, Samsung R&D Institute India-Bangalore; Chair, 3GPP SA WG3
nodes.description: Elected chair of 3GPP's security working group (SA WG3) in 2025.

nodes.name: CAICT (China Academy of Information and Communications Technology)
nodes.description: MIIT's research institute for telecoms policy and standards. Leads China's IMT-2030 (6G) Promotion Group and co-hosts the annual 6G Development Conference in Beijing.

nodes.name: MIIT (China Ministry of Industry and Information Technology)
nodes.description: China's industry and telecoms ministry. Set up the IMT-2030 (6G) Promotion Group in 2019, granted it 6 GHz (6,425 to 7,125 MHz) 6G trial spectrum in May 2026, and launched a ministry-provincial 6G pilot program (June 2026). In November 2026 approved eight pilot regions: Beijing, Hebei, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Anhui, Hubei and Guangdong. In November 2026 approved eight pilot regions: Beijing, Hebei, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Anhui, Hubei and Guangdong.

nodes.name: China Mobile Research Institute (Beijing)
nodes.description: China Mobile's R&D arm. Runs a 6G open laboratory in Beijing and an open, interoperable Sub-7 GHz 6G baseband prototype that partners can test against. Validated a U6G (upper 6 GHz) prototype base station and terminal with Qualcomm (2026). Leads the Beijing 6G Application Innovation Laboratory in Changping (2026).

nodes.name: ZGC Institute of Ubiquitous-X Innovation and Applications
nodes.description: Beijing research institute (Zhongguancun Pan-Institute). Built a cloud-native 6G prototype with China Mobile, exceeding 8 Gbps per user, and co-developed China Mobile's Sub-7 GHz 6G baseband prototype.

nodes.name: Tsinghua University
nodes.description: Beijing university. Department of Electronic Engineering researches semantic communications, AI-assisted wireless and 6G space-air-ground-sea coverage.

nodes.name: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications (BUPT)
nodes.description: Beijing telecoms university. Professor Zhang Ping's team built what it calls the world's first field test network for 6G communication and AI integration (2024), showing semantic communication on 4G infrastructure. Researches AI-native air interfaces and semantic communication for non-terrestrial networks.

nodes.name: Purple Mountain Laboratories (PMLabs)
nodes.address: Purple Mountain Science City, Jiangning, Nanjing, China
nodes.description: Nanjing 6G research institution, founded 2018. Pioneered cell-free radio access networks. Unveiled a field test network for 6G communication, intelligence and sensing (2025, drone sensing) and launched China's first Pre-6G test network in Nanjing (April 2026).

nodes.name: Southeast University (National Mobile Communications Research Laboratory)
nodes.description: Nanjing university whose National Mobile Communications Research Laboratory, directed by You Xiaohu, works closely with Purple Mountain Laboratories on 6G channel modelling, cell-free networks and terahertz.

nodes.name: ZTE Corporation
nodes.description: Shenzhen telecoms equipment maker. Showed GigaMIMO, a U6G (6,425 to 7,125 MHz) 6G prototype with 2,000+ antenna elements, at MWC 2026, and field-trialled it with China Mobile. First to verify dynamic reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) with China Mobile Research Institute (2022). Participant in China's 6G technical trials.

nodes.name: Nokia Shanghai Bell
nodes.description: Nokia's joint venture in China, based in Shanghai. Participant in China's national 6G technical trials.

nodes.name: Wang Zhiqin
nodes.role: Head, IMT-2030 (6G) Promotion Group; Vice President, CAICT
nodes.description: Leads China's 6G promotion group. Has said Nokia Shanghai Bell, Ericsson, China Mobile, China Telecom, China Unicom, Huawei, ZTE, vivo and Inspur took part in China's 6G technical trials.

nodes.name: Du Ying
nodes.role: Deputy Director, Wireless and Mobile Communications Research Institute, CAICT
nodes.description: CAICT wireless lead; projects a 1-trillion-yuan Chinese 6G industry by 2035.

nodes.name: Huang Yuhong
nodes.description: Heads China Mobile Research Institute; spoke on the 2026 U6G 6G validation with Qualcomm.

nodes.name: Liu Guangyi
nodes.role: Chief Expert, China Mobile; Chief Scientist, ZGC Institute of Ubiquitous-X Innovation and Applications
nodes.description: Has led China Mobile's 6G R&D since 2018. NGMN board member and co-chair of the 6G Alliance of Network AI (6GANA).

nodes.name: Chih-Lin I
nodes.role: Chief Scientist, Wireless Technologies, China Mobile
nodes.description: China Mobile's chief wireless scientist; argues AI is the most transformative part of 6G.

nodes.name: Zhang Ping
nodes.role: Professor, Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications
nodes.description: Leads BUPT's semantic communication and 6G intellicise network research, including the 2024 6G field test network.

nodes.name: Zhijin Qin
nodes.role: Department of Electronic Engineering, Tsinghua University
nodes.description: Researches semantic communications for 6G.

nodes.name: You Xiaohu
nodes.role: Director, National Mobile Communications Research Laboratory, Southeast University; Academician, Chinese Academy of Sciences
nodes.description: Led China's national 5G research project. Since 2018 has led Purple Mountain Laboratories' cell-free radio access network work for 6G.

nodes.name: Huang Yongming
nodes.role: Director, Pervasive Communication Research Center, Purple Mountain Laboratories
nodes.description: Leads Purple Mountain Laboratories' 6G field test work on integrated sensing and cell-free networks.

nodes.name: Cheng-Xiang Wang
nodes.role: Dean, School of Information Science and Engineering, Southeast University; Professor, Purple Mountain Laboratories
nodes.description: 6G channel measurement and modelling researcher; built the Southeast University-Purple Mountain Laboratories 6G pervasive channel simulator.

nodes.name: Nokia Oulu campus
nodes.description: Nokia's research and manufacturing campus in Oulu, opened in 2025 to build 5G and 6G radio networks for the AI era.

nodes.name: Nokia Bell Labs Finland (Espoo)
nodes.description: Nokia Bell Labs' Finnish site, home of Radio Systems Research Finland. Led the EU 6G flagship projects Hexa-X and Hexa-X-II (Nokia overall lead, Ericsson technical manager). Founding member of 6G Finland.

nodes.name: Business Finland
nodes.description: Finland's innovation funding agency. Ran the 6G Bridge program (2022 to 2026, EUR 130 million) for 5G-Advanced and 6G, and awarded Nokia EUR 40 million for AI-driven 6G and defence network R&D (June 2026). Runs joint 6G calls with South Korea and Sweden.

nodes.name: 6G Finland
nodes.description: National coalition of Finnish 6G R&D organisations, founded 2022 by universities (Oulu, Aalto, Helsinki, Tampere, LUT, Oulu UAS), Nokia Bell Labs, VTT, the Finnish Defence Research Agency and BusinessOulu. Published Finland's 6G roadmap for 2025 to 2028.

nodes.name: Aalto University
nodes.description: Espoo university. Long-standing Nokia partner: Nokia is donating EUR 1.5 million and funding about EUR 1.3 million a year of joint R&D in AI, 6G, resilient networks and semiconductors (November 2026). Partner in 6G-FUWIRI sub-THz research infrastructure and in Hexa-X-II.

nodes.name: VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland
nodes.description: Finland's state-owned applied research centre (Espoo and Oulu). Develops 6G hardware (antennas, RF front-ends to 300 GHz, photonics) and satellite-terrestrial networks. Coordinated the 6G-SatMTC satellite project with the University of Oulu, Nokia, Keysight and others.

nodes.name: Tampere University (Wireless Communications)
nodes.description: Founding member of 6G Finland. Wireless research on physical-layer algorithms, integrated sensing and communications, positioning and sub-THz radio. Partner in 6G-FUWIRI and in the Oulu-led RF ECO3 project.

nodes.name: University of Helsinki
nodes.description: Founding member of 6G Finland; computer science research on edge intelligence and networks.

nodes.name: CINET Flagship (Connected Intelligence and Networks for Resilient Society)
nodes.description: New Research Council of Finland flagship on connected intelligence and networks for a resilient society, from 2027. Aalto University is a partner.

nodes.name: 6G Rocket (AI-RAN project)
nodes.description: Two-year AI-RAN development project under the 6G Flagship, led by the University of Oulu from early 2026. DNA is the only operator taking part; the City of Oulu is also involved.

nodes.name: DNA
nodes.description: Finnish mobile operator owned by Telenor. The only operator in the University of Oulu's 6G Rocket AI-RAN project (2026).

nodes.name: Ericsson Finland (Jorvas)
nodes.description: Ericsson's Finnish R&D site, with around 700 staff, working on network security, cloud, 5G and 6G research and standardisation.

nodes.name: Traficom (Finnish Transport and Communications Agency)
nodes.description: Finland's telecoms regulator. Co-chairs the 6G subgroup of the EU Radio Spectrum Policy Group, which prepares Europe's 6G spectrum roadmaps.

nodes.name: Mikko Uusitalo
nodes.role: Head of Research Department, Radio Systems Research Finland, and Bell Labs Finland Site Lead, Nokia Bell Labs
nodes.description: Led the EU 6G flagship projects Hexa-X and Hexa-X-II (2023 to 2025). Industry co-chair of 6G Finland. Chair of the Nokia Foundation board.

nodes.name: Mikko Hautala
nodes.role: Head of Geopolitical and Government Relations and Country Senior Officer for Finland, Nokia
nodes.description: Nokia's senior figure in Finland; commented on Business Finland's EUR 40 million 6G and defence R&D award (2026).

nodes.name: Jaakko Sauvola
nodes.role: Ecosystem Director, 6G Flagship, University of Oulu; Co-Chair, 6G Finland
nodes.description: Leads the 6G Flagship's ecosystem and co-creation work and co-chairs the national 6G Finland coalition.

nodes.name: Markku Juntti
nodes.role: Professor, Centre for Wireless Communications, University of Oulu
nodes.description: Leads the 6G Flagship's Wireless Connectivity research area. IEEE Fellow.

nodes.name: Mehdi Bennis
nodes.description: 6G Flagship researcher on AI-native wireless and edge intelligence. IEEE Fellow (2020).

nodes.name: Dileepa Marasinghe
nodes.role: AI-RAN Research Manager, 6G Flagship, University of Oulu
nodes.description: Leads the 6G Flagship's AI-RAN team, working with NVIDIA on sensor-driven digital twins for AI-RAN.

nodes.name: Hannu Nikurautio
nodes.role: Research Director, 6G Test Centre, University of Oulu
nodes.description: Runs the University of Oulu's 6G Test Centre, a NATO DIANA test centre.

nodes.name: Hirley Alves
nodes.description: Co-leads 6G-FISRE, the joint Finnish-Swedish 6G resilience program with KTH.

nodes.name: Pekka Rantala
nodes.role: Head of 6G Bridge Program, Business Finland
nodes.description: Led Business Finland's EUR 130 million 6G Bridge program (2022 to 2026) and its international 6G calls.

nodes.name: Janne Järvinen
nodes.role: Mission Lead, Digital Native Finland, Business Finland; Co-Chair, 6G Finland
nodes.description: Co-chairs 6G Finland and leads Business Finland's Digital Native Finland mission.

nodes.name: Katsuyuki Haneda
nodes.role: Professor, Department of Electronics and Nanoengineering, Aalto University
nodes.description: Leads Aalto's antennas and propagation research on millimetre-wave and sub-THz radio, including Hexa-X-II sub-THz work.

nodes.name: Marko Höyhtyä
nodes.description: Leads VTT's satellite-terrestrial 6G research; coordinated the 6G-SatMTC project.

nodes.name: Mikko Valkama
nodes.description: Tampere University's contact for 6G Finland; leads wireless research on physical layer and sensing.

nodes.name: Heidi Himmanen
nodes.role: Chief Advisor, Traficom; Co-Chair, RSPG 6G subgroup
nodes.description: Co-chairs the EU Radio Spectrum Policy Group's 6G subgroup.

nodes.name: IMDA (Infocomm Media Development Authority)
nodes.description: Singapore's digital and telecoms regulator and development agency. With the National Research Foundation, is investing close to S$70 million in the Future Communications Research and Development Program (FCP), Singapore's national 6G program. Sets Singapore's telecoms standards.

nodes.name: National Research Foundation, Singapore (NRF)
nodes.description: Singapore's national research funder. Co-funds the Future Communications Research and Development Program with IMDA.

nodes.name: Future Communications Research and Development Programme (FCP)
nodes.description: Singapore's first national future communications and 6G program, launched 2021 with close to S$70 million from IMDA and NRF. Hosted by SUTD and directed by Professor Tony Quek. Runs the Future Communications Connectivity Lab at SUTD and the Future Communications Translation Lab at SIT, awards research and translation grants, and has a 6G MoU with Finland's 6G Flagship.

nodes.name: Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD)
nodes.description: Hosts the FCP and its Future Communications Connectivity Lab, launched in 2022 as Southeast Asia's first physical 6G lab. Hosts the MediaTek-SUTD Joint Laboratory (S$34 million, from April 2026) on non-terrestrial networks, AI-native radio access and energy-efficient networks.

nodes.name: Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT)
nodes.address: SIT Punggol Campus, Punggol Digital District, Singapore
nodes.description: Hosts the FCP's Future Communications Translation Lab (since 2021), which runs 5G testbeds (including Open RAN) at Punggol for translation of 5G and future communications technologies.

nodes.name: Nanyang Technological University (NTU Singapore)
nodes.description: FCP partner university. Its Centre for Advanced Robotics Technology Innovation (CARTIN) works with Ericsson and KTH on AI-powered 6G positioning for autonomous systems (from 2026).

nodes.name: National University of Singapore (NUS)
nodes.description: FCP partner university; Professor Biplab Sikdar is an FCP co-PI.

nodes.name: KTH Royal Institute of Technology
nodes.description: Stockholm university. Leads AI and algorithm research in Ericsson's Trustworthy 6G Positioning project with NTU (2026). Co-leads the Finnish-Swedish 6G-FISRE resilience program with the University of Oulu.

nodes.name: Tony Quek
nodes.role: Director, Future Communications Research and Development Program (FCP); Associate Provost (AI and Digital Innovation), SUTD
nodes.description: Leads Singapore's national 6G program and SUTD's O-RAN and AI-RAN work. Also heads SIT's Future Communications Translation Lab. IEEE Fellow.

nodes.name: Park Jihong
nodes.role: Associate Professor, SUTD; Lead, MediaTek-SUTD Joint Laboratory
nodes.description: Leads the MediaTek-SUTD 6G joint lab, researching how 6G networks can help robots and autonomous systems cooperate.

nodes.name: Chin Woon Hau
nodes.description: Oversees Singapore's telecoms standards and chairs IMDA's Telecommunications Standards Advisory Committee. Speaker at the IEEE 6G Summit 2026.

nodes.name: Ong Chen Hui
nodes.role: Assistant Chief Executive, Business and Technology Group, IMDA
nodes.description: Leads IMDA's work on 5G, 6G, AI and quantum-safe communications.

nodes.name: Lew Chuen Hong
nodes.description: Co-chairs the FCP Steering Committee.

nodes.name: Xie Lihua
nodes.role: Director, Centre for Advanced Robotics Technology Innovation (CARTIN); President’s Chair in Control Engineering, NTU
nodes.description: Leads NTU's robotics centre, which contributes sensor fusion and localisation to the Ericsson-NTU-KTH 6G positioning project.

nodes.name: Biplab Sikdar
nodes.role: Head, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, NUS; FCP Co-PI
nodes.description: FCP co-principal investigator for NUS.

nodes.name: Guan Yong Liang
nodes.role: Associate Vice President (Infrastructure and Programs), NTU; FCP Co-PI
nodes.description: FCP co-principal investigator for NTU.

nodes.name: Karl H. Johansson
nodes.description: KTH lead in the Ericsson-NTU-KTH Trustworthy 6G Positioning project.

nodes.name: EPSRC (Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council, UKRI)
nodes.address: Polaris House, North Star Avenue, Swindon
nodes.description: UK Research and Innovation's engineering and physical sciences council. Funds the UK's future telecoms hubs (TITAN, CHEDDAR, HASC, JOINER and the Federated Telecoms Hubs) through the Future Connectivity Hubs Evolution Program with DSIT, and funds the National 6G Radio Systems Facility at Sheffield.

nodes.name: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT)
nodes.description: UK government department for telecoms and digital infrastructure. Co-funds the future connectivity hubs with EPSRC, funded the REASON and TUDOR 6G projects (about £12m each) and funds the £80m UK Telecoms Lab.

nodes.name: Federated Telecoms Hubs (FTH)
nodes.description: Umbrella that links the UK's EPSRC telecoms research hubs (TITAN, CHEDDAR, HASC) and the JOINER experimentation platform, handling commercialisation, standards and industry engagement. Part of the Future Connectivity Hubs Evolution Program, which allows up to about £97.6m full economic cost across the five hubs (EPSRC funds 80%).

nodes.name: TITAN (Platform Driving the Ultimate Connectivity)
nodes.address: Electrical Engineering Division, 9 JJ Thomson Avenue, Cambridge
nodes.description: EPSRC telecoms hub on the 'network of networks', led by the University of Cambridge and directed by Professor Harald Haas. Covers AI for networks, radio, optical wireless, fibre, non-terrestrial and quantum networks across around 20 partner universities.

nodes.name: CHEDDAR (Communications Hub for Empowering Distributed clouD computing Applications and Research)
nodes.address: Department of Computing, Imperial College London, South Kensington
nodes.description: EPSRC telecoms hub led by Imperial College London (Professor Julie McCann) with Cranfield, Durham, Glasgow, Leeds and York. Researches telco cloud, distributed computing, network programmability, sensing and security for 6G.

nodes.name: HASC (Hub in All-Spectrum Connectivity)
nodes.address: Department of Engineering Science, Parks Road, Oxford
nodes.description: EPSRC telecoms hub led by the University of Oxford (Professor Dominic O'Brien), with Belfast, Bristol, Cambridge, Imperial, Southampton, Strathclyde and UCL. Researches how to combine wired and wireless spectrum, from radio to optical, into end-to-end connectivity.

nodes.name: JOINER (Joint Open Infrastructure for Networks Research)
nodes.address: Smart Internet Lab, University of Bristol
nodes.description: UK-wide 6G experimentation platform led by the University of Bristol's Smart Internet Lab. A dedicated network links labs and testbeds at partner universities and research organisations, including Digital Catapult (from 2025); Trinity College Dublin was its first international connection.

nodes.name: University of Cambridge
nodes.description: Leads the TITAN telecoms hub. Home of Professor Harald Haas's LiFi and optical wireless research.

nodes.name: Imperial College London
nodes.description: Leads the CHEDDAR telecoms hub on cloud and distributed computing for 6G.

nodes.name: University of Oxford
nodes.address: Department of Engineering Science, Parks Road, Oxford
nodes.description: Leads the HASC telecoms hub on all-spectrum (wired and wireless) connectivity.

nodes.name: University of Bristol (Smart Internet Lab)
nodes.address: Merchant Venturers Building, Woodland Road, Bristol
nodes.description: Its Smart Internet Lab, directed by Professor Dimitra Simeonidou, leads the JOINER national 6G experimentation platform and the DSIT-funded REASON open 6G networks project.

nodes.name: University of Sheffield (National 6G Radio Systems Facility)
nodes.address: Department of Electronic and Electrical Engineering, Sheffield
nodes.description: Hosts the UKRI National 6G Radio Systems Facility, the UK's first national 6G research facility (launched July 2024, EPSRC-funded, directed by Professor Timothy O'Farrell). Supports research on waveforms, RF and signal processing up to sub-THz, built on Keysight equipment.

nodes.name: National Physical Laboratory (NPL)
nodes.description: The UK's national measurement institute. Operates the UK Telecoms Lab in Solihull on behalf of DSIT.

nodes.name: UK Telecoms Lab (UKTL)
nodes.description: National telecoms security lab established by DSIT (£80m) and operated by NPL. Operators and vendors test the security, resilience and interoperability of telecoms equipment before UK deployment.

nodes.name: Digital Catapult
nodes.description: UK deep tech innovation agency with vendor-neutral 5G and Open RAN testbeds. One of the first sites connected to JOINER (2025), adding its network orchestration system. REASON partner working on 6G architecture.

nodes.name: BT Group
nodes.description: UK operator. Its Adastral Park research campus hosts 6G, upper 6 GHz spectrum and quantum-secure communications work. Partner in the REASON and TUDOR 6G projects; joined Nokia, NVIDIA and Qualcomm 6G initiatives at MWC 2026.

nodes.name: Harald Haas
nodes.role: Van Eck Professor of Engineering, University of Cambridge; Director, TITAN Hub
nodes.description: Pioneer of LiFi (optical wireless communications). Leads the TITAN 'network of networks' hub and the Federated Telecoms Hubs' push to connect academic research with industry.

nodes.name: Dimitra Simeonidou
nodes.role: Director, Smart Internet Lab and Founding Director, Bristol Digital Futures Institute, University of Bristol
nodes.description: Leads the JOINER national 6G experimentation platform and the DSIT REASON open 6G networks project. Specialist in optical and programmable networks. FREng.

nodes.name: Timothy O’Farrell
nodes.role: Professor of Wireless Communication, University of Sheffield; Director, National 6G Radio Systems Facility
nodes.description: Royal Academy of Engineering Research Chair developing waveforms for 6G's wide frequency range. FREng.

nodes.name: Yue Wang
nodes.role: Head of 6G and Advanced Network Research, Samsung R&D Institute UK
nodes.description: Leads Samsung UK's research on 5G and 6G system architecture, AI-native networks and O-RAN. Chairs UKTIN's AI expert working group.

nodes.name: Julie McCann
nodes.role: Professor, Department of Computing, Imperial College London; Lead, CHEDDAR Hub
nodes.description: Leads the CHEDDAR telecoms hub on cloud and distributed computing for 6G.

nodes.name: Dominic O’Brien
nodes.role: Professor of Engineering Science, University of Oxford; Lead, HASC Hub
nodes.description: Leads the HASC hub on combining wired and wireless spectrum.

nodes.name: CSIRO Data61
nodes.description: Digital research arm of CSIRO, Australia's national science agency. Ran Australia's 6G security research program for the Department of Home Affairs (2022 to mid-2025), covering privacy, secure protocols, network software and spectrum, and built a radio frequency test and collaboration platform. Published 'Security and privacy in 6G mobile' (October 2025).

nodes.name: Department of Home Affairs (Australia)
nodes.description: Australian government department. Funded CSIRO's three-year 6G and next-generation telecoms security research program.

nodes.name: University of Technology Sydney (UTS)
nodes.description: Home of the Global Big Data Technologies Centre (GBDTC) and its 5G/6G Wireless Communications and IoT Networking Lab, led by Distinguished Professor Jay Guo. Signed a beyond-6G, quantum and robotics MoU with the University of Oulu (November 2025) to set up a joint institute, and opened a wireless lab with Keysight (2026). Co-leads the NSW Connectivity Innovation Network.

nodes.name: University of Sydney
nodes.description: Its Centre for IoT and Telecommunications, led by ARC Laureate Fellow Professor Branka Vucetic, researches 5G and 6G wireless, low-latency communications, wireless control and edge computing. Co-leads the NSW Connectivity Innovation Network.

nodes.name: Connectivity Innovation Network (CIN)
nodes.description: NSW Government connectivity research network, launched 2021 by the NSW Telco Authority and the Office of the NSW Chief Scientist & Engineer. Jointly led by UTS and the University of Sydney. Runs the annual Australian Beyond 5G Connectivity Summit (2026 theme: AI-native networks for Australia's 6G future).

nodes.name: Swinburne University of Technology
nodes.description: Hosts the 6G Research and Innovation Laboratory, funded by Telstra, ARPANSA, the NHMRC-funded Australian Centre for Electromagnetic Bioeffects Research and Swinburne. Works on millimetre-wave devices, electromagnetic simulation and radiofrequency exposure safety.

nodes.name: ARPANSA (Australian Radiation Protection and Nuclear Safety Agency)
nodes.description: Australia's radiation safety regulator. Co-funds and shares staff and facilities with Swinburne's 6G Research and Innovation Laboratory for research on high-frequency radio exposure.

nodes.name: Monash University
nodes.description: Its Department of Electrical and Computer Systems Engineering (Professor Malin Premaratne) developed quantum-inspired optical wireless technology for 6G with the University of Melbourne (2026).

nodes.name: University of Melbourne
nodes.description: Professor Thas Nirmalathas's optical wireless research contributed to quantum-inspired optical phased arrays for 6G with Monash (2026).

nodes.name: Telstra
nodes.description: Australia's largest operator. Signed a 6G letter of intent with Ericsson (May 2026) covering 3GPP standards, research and trials at Ericsson's Swedish testbed and Telstra's Gold Coast Innovation Centre. Has run upper 6 GHz trials at Anglesea, Victoria, and funds Swinburne's 6G lab.

nodes.name: Optus
nodes.address: Optus Sydney campus, Macquarie Park, Sydney
nodes.description: Australian operator. With Nokia and a MediaTek test device, reached 3.5 Gbps on a smartphone using 200 MHz of upper 6 GHz spectrum at its Sydney campus (August 2026), with coverage similar to its 5G 3.5 GHz layer.

nodes.name: ACMA (Australian Communications and Media Authority)
nodes.description: Australia's spectrum regulator. Deciding the future of the upper 6 GHz band and other 6G candidate bands through its Five-year Spectrum Outlook.

nodes.name: AMTA (Australian Mobile Telecommunications Association)
nodes.description: Industry body for Australia's mobile operators, vendors and retailers. Lobbies ACMA on spectrum for 6G, including upper 6 GHz, 600 MHz and licence renewal pricing.

nodes.name: Jay Guo
nodes.role: Distinguished Professor; Director, Global Big Data Technologies Centre, UTS
nodes.description: Antenna and 6G wireless researcher leading UTS's partnership with Finland's 6G Flagship (MoU signed November 2025).

nodes.name: Hajime Suzuki
nodes.description: Lead author of CSIRO's 'Security and privacy in 6G mobile' report (2025).

nodes.name: Chandra Thapa
nodes.description: Works on CSIRO's 6G security research, combining physical testbeds with simulation to close security, virtualisation and standards gaps.

nodes.name: Ming Ding
nodes.role: Group Leader, Privacy Technology Group, CSIRO
nodes.description: Researches privacy and safety risks in 6G, including radio sensing.

nodes.name: Ali Yavari
nodes.role: Associate Professor; Director, 6G Research and Innovation Laboratory, Swinburne University of Technology
nodes.description: Leads Swinburne's 6G lab. Previously researched at CSIRO's Data61 and KTH; has worked with Ericsson, Telstra, Optus and CSIRO.

nodes.name: Andrew Wood
nodes.description: Lead scientist on Swinburne and ARPANSA research into the safety of high-frequency radio waves for 5G and 6G.

nodes.name: Yonghui Li
nodes.role: Professor; Director, Wireless Engineering Laboratory, University of Sydney
nodes.description: Researches 6G low-latency communications, IoT and wireless networks. Technical co-director of the NSW Connectivity Innovation Network.

nodes.name: Branka Vucetic
nodes.role: ARC Laureate Fellow; Professor; Lead, Centre for IoT and Telecommunications, University of Sydney
nodes.description: Leads Sydney's Centre for IoT and Telecommunications, working on AI for 6G, channel coding and wireless control.

nodes.name: Thas Nirmalathas
nodes.description: Optical wireless communications researcher. Co-developed quantum-inspired optical phased arrays for 6G with Monash (2026).

nodes.name: Malin Premaratne
nodes.role: Professor, Department of Electrical and Computer Systems Engineering, Monash University
nodes.description: Quantum device researcher. Co-developed quantum-inspired optical wireless technology for fibre-like indoor 6G links (2026).

nodes.name: Channa Seneviratne
nodes.role: Executive, Technology Engagement and Advancement, Global Networks and Technology, Telstra
nodes.description: Leads Telstra's network technology innovation, strategy and architecture teams, and its 'network as a product' approach. Led Telstra's 5G launch.

nodes.name: Sri Amirthalingam
nodes.description: Leads Optus's 6G research program, including the 2026 upper 6 GHz trial with Nokia.

nodes.name: Anna Gomez
nodes.role: Commissioner, Federal Communications Commission (holdover since July 2026)
nodes.description: FCC Commissioner since September 2023 and the Commission's only Democratic member. Her five-year term expired in June 2026 and she continues to serve in a holdover capacity. Previously Deputy Administrator of NTIA, Deputy Chief of the FCC International Bureau and a telecoms lawyer in private practice.

nodes.name: Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS)
nodes.address: 1616 Rhode Island Avenue NW, Washington, DC
nodes.description: Washington DC policy think tank. Publishes analysis on technology, telecoms and trusted digital infrastructure policy.

nodes.name: Steve Lang
nodes.role: Non-resident Senior Associate, CSIS; Senior Advisor, Crest Hill Advisors; former US Coordinator for International Communications and Information Policy (Ambassador), State Department
nodes.description: Retired US diplomat (Ambassador Stephan A. Lang). Led State Department diplomacy on international telecoms standards and trusted ICT infrastructure as US Coordinator for International Communications and Information Policy (May 2024 to July 2025), after serving as Deputy Assistant Secretary from November 2022. Member of SpectrumX working groups.

nodes.name: SpaceX (Starlink)
nodes.description: Launch and satellite company that runs Starlink. Its direct-to-cell service, renamed Starlink Mobile in 2026, works with operator partners worldwide. Bought EchoStar's AWS-4 and H-block spectrum (about $17bn, 2025) for a next-generation direct-to-cell constellation due to start launching in 2027, targeting up to 150 Mbps. Engaging in 3GPP standards work on 6G non-terrestrial networks. Acquired xAI in February 2026.

nodes.name: One NZ
nodes.description: New Zealand operator and Starlink direct-to-cell partner.

nodes.name: Salt Mobile
nodes.description: Swiss operator and Starlink direct-to-cell partner.

nodes.name: Entel
nodes.description: Operator in Chile and Peru and Starlink direct-to-cell partner in both countries.

nodes.name: Kyivstar (VEON)
nodes.description: Ukrainian operator, part of VEON. Launched Europe's first Starlink direct-to-cell service in November 2025.

nodes.name: Virgin Media O2
nodes.description: UK operator and Starlink direct-to-cell partner, with a satellite service planned for 2026.

nodes.name: Airtel Africa
nodes.description: Pan-African operator. Starlink direct-to-cell partner, with service planned across 14 African countries.

nodes.name: Elon Musk
nodes.description: Leads SpaceX, including Starlink and, since February 2026, xAI.

nodes.name: Gwynne Shotwell
nodes.description: Leads SpaceX's commercial strategy, including Starlink Mobile direct-to-cell and the EchoStar spectrum deal.

nodes.name: Michael Nicolls
nodes.description: Leads Starlink. Launched the Starlink Mobile brand and its second-generation direct-to-cell plans at MWC 2026.

nodes.name: Hamid Akhavan
nodes.description: Led EchoStar's sale of AWS-4 and H-block spectrum to SpaceX (2025).

nodes.name: University of Mississippi School of Law (Center for Air and Space Law)
nodes.description: Ole Miss law school. Its Center for Air and Space Law runs an LL.M. in Air and Space Law and publishes on international space treaties and commercial space activity.

nodes.name: University of Nebraska College of Law (Space, Cyber and Telecommunications Law)
nodes.description: Nebraska Law runs one of the main US space, cyber and telecommunications law programs, with an advisory board including satellite industry figures.

nodes.name: Ruth Pritchard-Kelly
nodes.role: Adjunct Professor, Center for Air and Space Law, University of Mississippi; Principal, RPK Advisors
nodes.description: Satellite regulatory policy expert with over 30 years' experience. Former Senior Advisor for Regulatory and Space Policy at OneWeb (now part of Eutelsat). Earlier worked at O3b (now SES) and American Mobile Satellite Corporation. Teaches space and telecoms law at Ole Miss and is linked to Nebraska's Space, Cyber and Telecommunications Law program.

nodes.name: Spark New Zealand
nodes.address: Spark City, 167 Victoria Street West, Auckland
nodes.description: New Zealand's largest operator by mobile share. Launched satellite-to-mobile on SpaceX's Starlink direct-to-cell network in April 2026. Signed the GSMA Open Gateway MoU with One NZ and 2degrees (March 2026) to build shared network APIs. Co-owns the Rural Connectivity Group.

nodes.name: 2degrees
nodes.description: New Zealand mobile operator. Proposed in August 2026 to combine its radio access network with One NZ's in a jointly owned wholesale company (RANCo), citing faster access to technologies such as 6G. Co-owns the Rural Connectivity Group and signed the GSMA Open Gateway MoU.

nodes.name: RANCo (One NZ and 2degrees RAN joint venture)
nodes.description: Proposed 50/50 joint venture combining One NZ's and 2degrees' radio access network equipment into a wholesale company that sells capacity back to both. Each operator keeps its own spectrum, core network, fibre backhaul and satellite assets. Needs Commerce Commission and Overseas Investment Office approval; completion targeted for the first half of 2027.

nodes.name: Rural Connectivity Group (RCG)
nodes.description: Joint venture of Spark, One NZ and 2degrees that builds and runs a shared rural mobile network (600 sites by 2026), contracted by the government's Crown Infrastructure Partners (now National Infrastructure Funding and Financing).

nodes.name: Tait Communications
nodes.description: Christchurch-headquartered critical communications company. Its TAIT AXIOM range converges land mobile radio with LTE, satellite and Wi-Fi. Building New Zealand's 500-site digital LMR network for the Public Safety Network. Works closely with the University of Canterbury's Wireless Research Centre.

nodes.name: MiMOMax Wireless
nodes.description: Christchurch company that applies MIMO to narrowband licensed radio channels, making highly spectrum-efficient, low-latency links for utility SCADA and mission-critical networks. Works closely with the University of Canterbury's Wireless Research Centre.

nodes.name: University of Canterbury (Wireless Research Centre)
nodes.description: Home of the Wireless Research Centre, New Zealand's only research centre focused on wireless, which works with Tait, MiMOMax and avionics and defence partners on MIMO, software-defined radio and IoT. Its Communications Research Group (UCCRG) researches coding, space-time processing, smart antennas and cognitive radio.

nodes.name: University of Auckland
nodes.address: Faculty of Engineering, 20 Symonds Street, Auckland
nodes.description: Its telecommunications and electromagnetics group researches radio wave propagation in New Zealand environments, indoor wireless design, interference and microwave engineering.

nodes.name: Radio Spectrum Management (RSM), MBIE
nodes.description: Business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment that manages New Zealand's radio spectrum. Opened the lower 6 GHz band (5925 to 6425 MHz) to Wi-Fi and is monitoring international decisions on the upper 6 GHz band for mobile (IMT). Implements the 2022 Crown and Māori spectrum agreement with the Māori Spectrum Working Group.

nodes.name: GSMA
nodes.description: Global mobile operator association. Runs Open Gateway, a framework of standardised network APIs built on the CAMARA open-source project.

nodes.name: Ministry of Science and Technology (Vietnam)
nodes.description: Vietnam's ministry responsible for telecoms and spectrum, including the Vietnam Telecommunications Authority. Set up a 6G Steering Committee of regulators, spectrum managers, operators and universities to give Vietnamese firms early access to 6G and a role in global standards, ahead of a planned national rollout from 2030.

nodes.name: Viettel (Viettel High Tech)
nodes.description: Military-owned operator and equipment maker. Its Viettel High Tech arm became the first partner in Qualcomm's 6G Platform Early Access Program (July 2026) to research, design and manufacture 6G base stations, targeting Vietnam's first pre-commercial 6G call in early 2029. Also signed 6G deals with Intel, AMD and ID Quantique at MWC 2026.

nodes.name: VNPT (Vietnam Posts and Telecommunications Group)
nodes.description: State-owned Vietnamese operator. Its 2030 strategy positions it to pioneer 6G research, focusing on the 6G ecosystem, international partnerships and standards participation.

nodes.name: 6G-SANDBOX
nodes.description: Horizon Europe (SNS JU) project, coordinated by Keysight and launched in January 2023 with 16 partners, building pan-European 6G experimentation testbeds. Signed MoUs with ITRI (Taiwan), Universiti Malaya (2024) and the European Space Agency.

nodes.name: Universiti Malaya (UM)
nodes.description: Malaysia's oldest university. Signed an MoU with the Keysight-led 6G-SANDBOX project (July 2024) to connect its experimental networks to the European testbeds, and runs a two-year 5G/6G millimetre-wave research project with Keysight.

nodes.name: Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (Wireless Communication Centre)
nodes.description: Malaysia's Higher Institution Centre of Excellence (HICoE) for wireless communications since 2014. Researches 6G topics including vehicle-to-everything with Hanyang University (Korea) and intelligent reflecting surfaces.

nodes.name: MCMC (Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission)
nodes.description: Malaysia's communications regulator and spectrum manager.

nodes.name: Telkomsel
nodes.description: Indonesia's largest operator. Building 5G-Advanced as its bridge to 6G and exploring satellite integration. Signed a strategic partnership with ZTE at MWC 2026 that includes evaluating AI-native RAN.

nodes.name: Komdigi (Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs, Indonesia)
nodes.description: Indonesia's communications ministry and spectrum regulator. Says Indonesia needs new spectrum for 6G but is taking a 'wait and see' approach to choosing 6G bands, following international harmonisation. Hosted the 2026 ASEAN digital senior officials and spectrum working group meetings.

nodes.name: Telkom University
nodes.description: Its Advanced Communications Research Centre (AICOMS) runs wireless research, including a study with Komdigi.

nodes.name: AIS (Advanced Info Service)
nodes.description: Thailand's largest operator. Launched what it calls Southeast Asia's first 5G-Advanced network (2026) and works with Huawei and ZTE on AI-driven network operations and AI-enabled RAN. Runs a 5G innovation lab with Chulalongkorn University.

nodes.name: True Corporation
nodes.description: Thai operator (merged with dtac). Runs TrueLab@ChulaEngineering, a 5G innovation centre at Chulalongkorn University, and a quantum AI research partnership (2026).

nodes.name: Chulalongkorn University
nodes.description: Ran Thailand's first upper 6 GHz (6425 to 7125 MHz) mobile field test with test spectrum from the regulator NBTC (2023) and the country's first 5.5G field test (2025). Hosts 5G labs with AIS and True.

nodes.name: Globe Telecom
nodes.address: The Globe Tower, Bonifacio Global City, Taguig, Philippines
nodes.description: Leading Philippine operator. Launched Starlink Mobile direct-to-cell in 2026, Southeast Asia's first commercial service of its kind, after regulator NTC approval. Has an MoU with AST SpaceMobile (2022) and has trialled Lynk.

nodes.name: Smart Communications (PLDT)
nodes.description: PLDT's mobile arm. Partnered with AST SpaceMobile (MoU 2021; BlueWalker 3 test 2022) and has run direct-to-device field tests with Lynk Global in 2026.

nodes.name: DICT (Department of Information and Communications Technology, Philippines)
nodes.description: Philippine ICT department. Supports satellite direct-to-cell services to reach remote islands; direct-to-cell licences go through the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC).

nodes.name: Tao Duc Thang
nodes.description: Lieutenant General. Leads Viettel, which signed Qualcomm's first 6G Platform Early Access Program agreement (2026).

nodes.name: Nguyen Minh Quang
nodes.description: Signed the 6G Platform Early Access Program agreement with Qualcomm (July 2026).

nodes.name: Nguyen Anh Cuong
nodes.description: Public voice of Vietnam's 6G plans and the MST 6G Steering Committee.

nodes.name: Durga Malladi
nodes.role: EVP and General Manager, Qualcomm Technologies
nodes.description: Signed Qualcomm's 6G Platform Early Access Program agreement with Viettel High Tech (July 2026).

nodes.name: Michael Dieudonné
nodes.description: Coordinates the Horizon Europe 6G-SANDBOX testbed project and its MoUs with Asian partners. Keysight's representative on the 6G-IA Governing Board (2026 to 2029).

nodes.name: Norhudah Seman
nodes.role: Associate Professor; Director, Wireless Communication Centre, UTM
nodes.description: Leads UTM's wireless centre of excellence.

nodes.name: Adis Alifiawan
nodes.role: Director of Radio Frequency Spectrum, Satellite Orbits and Digital Infrastructure Standardisation, Komdigi
nodes.description: Leads Indonesia's 6G spectrum planning.

nodes.name: Wong Soon Nam
nodes.role: Director of Planning and Transformation, Telkomsel
nodes.description: Signed Telkomsel's strategic partnership with ZTE at MWC 2026.

nodes.name: Hexa-X-II (European 6G Flagship)
nodes.description: EU 6G flagship project (January 2023 to June 2025) under the Smart Networks and Services Joint Undertaking. Led by Nokia, with Ericsson as technical manager, and 43 partners including Aalto, Chalmers, Oulu, Orange, Siemens, imec and CTTC. Produced the European 6G system blueprint and was the top SNS JU project for 3GPP contributions.

nodes.name: Smart Networks and Services Joint Undertaking (SNS JU)
nodes.description: EU public-private partnership that funds Europe's 6G research and trials under Horizon Europe, including Hexa-X-II, 6G-SANDBOX and 6G-NTN. The 6G Industry Association (6G-IA) represents the private side.

nodes.name: Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR, Germany)
nodes.description: German research ministry (formerly BMBF). Funded four 6G research hubs from 2021 with up to €250 million, within a 6G program of up to €700 million. Since 2026 funds their successors as 6G transfer hubs (6G-life², xG-RIC, Open6GHub+, 6GEM+) and the 6G Platform Germany.

nodes.name: 6G-life² (TU Dresden and TU Munich)
nodes.description: German 6G transfer hub run by TU Dresden and TU Munich, focused on human-machine collaboration, collaborative robotics and computing. First phase from 2021 (€70 million); second phase 6G-life² (2026 to 2029) has €25 million from BMFTR. Supports spin-offs through the launchhub42 incubator in Dresden.

nodes.name: xG-RIC (formerly 6G-RIC), Berlin
nodes.description: German 6G transfer hub for connected medicine and future mobility, successor to 6G-RIC (2021 to 2025). Coordinated by Fraunhofer HHI with TU Berlin; partners include DLR, Charité, FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg and IHP. Covers integrated sensing and communication, collaborative robotics and resilient networks. With sister project xG-NOVA, around €40 million to 2029.

nodes.name: Open6GHub+
nodes.description: German 6G transfer hub (2026 to 2029), successor to Open6GHub. Coordinated by Hans D. Schotten (DFKI and RPTU) with FAU, Fraunhofer FOKUS, KIT, TU Darmstadt, RPTU, Bremen and Stuttgart. Focuses on AI across the 6G ecosystem, digital twins and 3D networks linking terrestrial, drone and non-terrestrial platforms.

nodes.name: 6GEM+ (RWTH Aachen and partners)
nodes.description: German 6G transfer hub 6GEM+ ('Value-Oriented 6G Communication Systems for the Networked Digital Industry', 2026 onwards), successor to 6GEM (2021 to 2025). Coordinated by RWTH Aachen with Ruhr University Bochum, TU Dortmund and Fraunhofer IPT and IML. Focus on industrial automation, logistics, mobility and rescue robotics. Funded by BMFTR with up to €25 million. Runs the 6GEMcubator start-up incubator.

nodes.name: Fraunhofer Heinrich Hertz Institute (HHI)
nodes.description: Fraunhofer institute for telecommunications. Coordinates the xG-RIC and xG-NOVA 6G transfer projects and joined the 6G Platform Germany consortium (2026).

nodes.name: Technische Universität Berlin
nodes.description: Partner in the xG-RIC 6G transfer hub and the 6G Platform Germany.

nodes.name: Technical University of Munich (TUM)
nodes.description: Runs the 6G-life² transfer hub with TU Dresden and leads the 6G Future Lab Bavaria.

nodes.name: German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence (DFKI)
nodes.description: Coordinates the Open6GHub+ 6G transfer hub, focusing on integrating AI across the 6G ecosystem.

nodes.name: RPTU Kaiserslautern-Landau
nodes.description: Technical university of Rhineland-Palatinate. Partner in Open6GHub+ and Hexa-X-II; its Professor Hans D. Schotten coordinates the second phase of the 6G Platform Germany.

nodes.name: RWTH Aachen University
nodes.description: Coordinates the 6GEM+ 6G transfer hub (Professor Haris Gačanin), as it did the 6GEM research hub from 2021.

nodes.name: Siemens
nodes.description: German industrial technology group. Partner in the Hexa-X-II 6G flagship.

nodes.name: German Aerospace Center (DLR)
