nodes.description: Germany's aerospace research centre. Partner in the xG-RIC 6G transfer hub.

nodes.name: PEPR Networks of the Future (Réseaux du Futur), France 2030
nodes.description: French national research program on 5G and 6G (launched July 2023, €65 million over six years from France 2030), co-led by CEA, CNRS and Institut Mines-Télécom. Covers end-to-end systems, technology building blocks and platforms, including environmental impact. Tasked with proposing a 'France 6G' platform.

nodes.name: CEA (including CEA-Leti)
nodes.description: French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission. Co-leads the PEPR Networks of the Future program.

nodes.name: CNRS (French National Centre for Scientific Research)
nodes.description: Co-leads the PEPR Networks of the Future program.

nodes.name: Institut Mines-Télécom (IMT)
nodes.description: French group of engineering schools including Télécom Paris. Co-leads the PEPR Networks of the Future program.

nodes.name: Orange
nodes.description: French operator. Partner in the Hexa-X-II 6G flagship.

nodes.name: Thales Alenia Space
nodes.description: Satellite manufacturer. Thales Alenia Space France leads technical coordination of the EU 6G-NTN project.

nodes.name: 6G-NTN (6G Non-Terrestrial Networks)
nodes.description: SNS JU project (2023 to 2025) to integrate satellite and other non-terrestrial networks into 6G and drive 3GPP standards. Coordinated by the University of Bologna; technical coordination by Thales Alenia Space France; partners across eight countries including CTTC. Succeeded by 6G-NTN2 NEXUS. Partners included Thales Alenia Space, Thales SIX and Thales DIS, Ericsson, Qualcomm, SES Techcom, Orange, Telit Cinterion, Greenerwave, Martel Innovate, Digital for Planet, DLR and CTTC.

nodes.name: University of Bologna
nodes.description: Coordinates the EU 6G-NTN project (Professor Alessandro Vanelli-Coralli).

nodes.name: CTTC (Centre Tecnològic de Telecomunicacions de Catalunya)
nodes.description: Catalan telecoms research centre. Partner in Hexa-X-II and 6G-NTN (space and resilient communications).

nodes.name: Luleå University of Technology
nodes.description: Swedish university. Partner in the Hexa-X-II 6G flagship.

nodes.name: imec
nodes.description: Belgian nanoelectronics research centre. Partner in the Hexa-X-II 6G flagship.

nodes.name: TNO
nodes.description: Dutch applied research organisation. Leads the Future Network Services 6G consortium.

nodes.name: Future Network Services (6G NL)
nodes.description: Dutch national 6G program led by TNO with around 60 partners in antennas, semiconductors, network software and mobile networks. Backed by up to €203 million from the National Growth Fund (€61 million phase 1 from 2024; €142 million phase 2 from 2026). Aims include the first fully wireless factory in the Netherlands.

nodes.name: Delft University of Technology
nodes.description: Partner in the Dutch Future Network Services 6G program.

nodes.name: Patrik Rugeland
nodes.description: Ericsson's technical manager role in the Hexa-X-II 6G flagship.

nodes.name: Frank Fitzek
nodes.role: Professor, Deutsche Telekom Chair of Communication Networks, TU Dresden
nodes.description: Coordinated the 6G-life research hub from 2021 and leads TU Dresden's part of 6G-life².

nodes.name: Holger Boche
nodes.role: Professor of Theoretical Information Technology, TUM; Head of 6G-life
nodes.description: Leads the 6G-life initiative and its TUM part.

nodes.name: Wolfgang Kellerer
nodes.role: Professor of Communication Networks, TUM; Head of 6G Future Lab Bavaria
nodes.description: Co-coordinates TUM's part of 6G-life.

nodes.name: Slawomir Stanczak
nodes.role: Head of Wireless Communications and Networks Department, Fraunhofer HHI; Professor, TU Berlin
nodes.description: Coordinates the xG-RIC and xG-NOVA 6G transfer projects.

nodes.name: Hans D. Schotten
nodes.role: Head of Intelligent Networks Research, DFKI; Professor, RPTU
nodes.description: Coordinates Open6GHub+ and the second phase of the 6G Platform Germany.

nodes.name: Dimitri Ktenas
nodes.role: Co-director, PEPR Networks of the Future (CEA)
nodes.description: Co-directs France's 5G and 6G research program for CEA.

nodes.name: Serge Verdeyme
nodes.role: Co-director, PEPR Networks of the Future (CNRS)
nodes.description: Co-directs France's 5G and 6G research program for CNRS.

nodes.name: Daniel Kofman
nodes.role: Co-director, PEPR Networks of the Future (IMT)
nodes.description: Co-directs France's 5G and 6G research program for Institut Mines-Télécom.

nodes.name: Alessandro Vanelli-Coralli
nodes.description: Coordinates the EU 6G-NTN project.

nodes.name: Bittium
nodes.description: Finnish secure and tactical communications company (Nasdaq Helsinki). Donated a tactical communications system to the University of Oulu's 6G Test Centre to support dual-use testing. Partner in the RF ECO3 6G radio project.

nodes.name: 6G Test Centre (University of Oulu)
nodes.description: Test facility within Finland's 6G Flagship and a designated NATO DIANA test centre. Focuses on civilian, dual-use and defence testing, including hybrid tactical and 6G networks. Industry contributors include Bittium, Keysight and Nokia.

nodes.name: RF ECO3 (Finland)
nodes.description: Business Finland Veturi ecosystem project on sustainable 6G radio systems, running to the end of 2027. Partners: Nokia, Bittium, CoreHW, SAAB, Optenni, Verkotan, Senfit, University of Oulu, Aalto University, Tampere University and VTT.

nodes.name: Cumucore
nodes.description: Finnish SME making 4G, 5G and 6G core network software for non-public industrial networks. Holds local spectrum licences in Finland and runs Aalto University's test network.

nodes.name: Elisa
nodes.description: Finnish operator. Deployed Europe's first commercial 5G Cloud RAN with Nokia (December 2024), which it describes as groundwork for 6G-era cloud-native networks.

nodes.name: EURECOM
nodes.description: French graduate school and research centre. Founded OpenAirInterface (OAI), the open-source 3GPP and O-RAN software stack used for 6G research.

nodes.name: OpenAirInterface Software Alliance
nodes.description: Non-profit that runs OpenAirInterface, the open-source RAN, core and UE software for 5G and 6G research. Grew out of EURECOM.

nodes.name: Sequans Communications
nodes.description: French maker of low-power 5G IoT modems. Partner in the Hexa-X-II 6G flagship, contributing on massive IoT for 6G.

nodes.name: Telefónica
nodes.description: Spanish operator with the largest operator share of SNS JU projects (more than 35 6G projects). Co-organised EuCNC & 6G Summit 2026 and leads the EURO-3C sovereign infrastructure initiative.

nodes.name: i2CAT Foundation
nodes.description: Catalan internet research foundation. Partner in the MultiX 6G sensing project.

nodes.name: Universidad Carlos III de Madrid (UC3M)
nodes.description: Coordinates the EU 6G projects MultiX (6G sensing, 2025 to 2027) and PAISES-6G, and the MiFuture network on ultra-massive MIMO.

nodes.name: MultiX (EU 6G sensing project)
nodes.description: SNS JU project (January 2025 to June 2027) on 6G networks that sense their surroundings, using integrated sensing and communication. Coordinated by UC3M with 17 partners from 7 countries, including Telefónica, Siemens, Intel, Apple, InterDigital, CNIT, IHP, i2CAT and IMDEA Networks.

nodes.name: IMDEA Networks Institute
nodes.description: Madrid research institute. Won four SNS JU 6G projects in 2026 (PROSPERO, PAISES-6G, IoT-ZERO, PRIME-6G). Builds a multi-band sensing platform for MultiX.

nodes.name: TIM (Telecom Italia)
nodes.description: Italian operator. Partner in RESTART, Italy's national 6G and telecoms research program.

nodes.name: CNIT (National Inter-University Consortium for Telecommunications)
nodes.description: Italian university telecoms consortium. Partner in RESTART and the EU MultiX and PAISES-6G projects.

nodes.name: Politecnico di Milano
nodes.description: Hosts RESTART's scientific direction. Runs open-air 6G experiments (FR1 to 251 GHz) and ran Europe's first upper 6 GHz trial (2023). Built an upper mid-band 6G prototyping platform with NYU and Pi-Radio.

nodes.name: RESTART (Italy national telecoms and 6G program)
nodes.description: Italy's largest public telecoms R&D program (€116 million, national recovery plan, 25 partners). Led by the University of Rome Tor Vergata with scientific direction at PoliMi. Partners include CNIT, TIM, Vodafone, Wind Tre, Ericsson, Leonardo and the University of Bologna.

nodes.name: University of Rome Tor Vergata
nodes.description: Lead proponent of the RESTART program.

nodes.name: Rohde & Schwarz
nodes.description: German test and measurement company. Partner in German 6G projects including 6G-ANNA. Researches THz 6G (D-band and H-band) with Fraunhofer HHI and IAF, and AI-native air interfaces.

nodes.name: Fraunhofer FOKUS
nodes.description: Fraunhofer institute for open communication systems. Partner in Open6GHub+ and took part in 6G-RIC and Open6GHub in the first phase.

nodes.name: Fraunhofer IAF
nodes.description: Fraunhofer institute for applied solid state physics. Took part in 6G-RIC; THz 6G research with Rohde & Schwarz and HHI.

nodes.name: Fraunhofer IIS
nodes.description: Fraunhofer institute for integrated circuits. Took part in the 6G-RIC hub.

nodes.name: Fraunhofer IZM
nodes.description: Fraunhofer institute for reliability and microintegration. Took part in the 6G-RIC hub.

nodes.name: IHP (Leibniz Institute for High Performance Microelectronics)
nodes.description: Leibniz microelectronics institute. Partner in the xG-RIC transfer hub and the EU MultiX project.

nodes.name: Ferdinand-Braun-Institut (FBH)
nodes.description: Leibniz institute for high-frequency technology. Took part in the 6G-RIC hub.

nodes.name: TU Dortmund University
nodes.description: Partner in 6GEM+ (Christian Wietfeld is site speaker). Its Centre for Entrepreneurship & Transfer is involved.

nodes.name: Ruhr University Bochum
nodes.description: Partner in 6GEM+ (site speaker Aydin Sezgin), focused on human-robot collaboration, XR and energy-efficient communication.

nodes.name: University of Duisburg-Essen
nodes.description: Partner in the first 6GEM research hub (2021 to 2025).

nodes.name: Fraunhofer IML
nodes.description: Fraunhofer institute for material flow and logistics. Partner in 6GEM and 6GEM+, leading logistics use cases.

nodes.name: Fraunhofer IPT
nodes.description: Fraunhofer institute for production technology. Partner in the 6GEM+ transfer hub.

nodes.name: 6GEMcubator
nodes.description: 6G start-up incubator spun off from the 6GEM hub, with RWTH Innovation, Cube 5 (Bochum) and TU concept (Dortmund). Regional contact point for the national StartUpConnect program.

nodes.name: launchhub42
nodes.description: Start-up incubator in Dresden set up in 2024 to support 6G and robotics spin-offs from 6G-life.

nodes.name: Antonio de la Oliva
nodes.role: Professor of Telematics Engineering, UC3M; Principal Investigator, MultiX
nodes.description: Leads the EU MultiX 6G sensing project.

nodes.name: Antonio Guzmán
nodes.role: Director of Innovation, CDO unit, Telefónica
nodes.description: Speaks for Telefónica on 6G architecture at EuCNC & 6G Summit 2026.

nodes.name: Antonio Capone
nodes.role: Professor, Politecnico di Milano; Scientific Coordinator, RESTART
nodes.description: Scientific coordinator of Italy's RESTART program.

nodes.name: Umberto Spagnolini
nodes.role: Professor, Politecnico di Milano; PI, RESTART 6G Wireless Networks
nodes.description: Leads RESTART's 6G wireless experimental platforms.

nodes.name: Thomas Magedanz
nodes.description: Co-author of the German 6G hubs' joint work.

nodes.name: Haris Gačanin
nodes.role: Professor, Chair of Distributed Signal Processing, RWTH Aachen; Coordinator, 6GEM
nodes.description: Coordinates the 6GEM hub and its 6GEM+ successor.

nodes.name: Christian Wietfeld
nodes.role: Professor, Chair of Communication Networks, TU Dortmund; 6GEM+ site speaker
nodes.description: Leads TU Dortmund's 6GEM+ team.

nodes.name: Aydin Sezgin
nodes.role: Professor of Digital Communication, Ruhr University Bochum; 6GEM+ site speaker
nodes.description: Leads Bochum's 6GEM+ work.

nodes.name: Fairwinds Technologies
nodes.description: Private company founded in 2016 that designs communications, networking and IT products for military, defence and civilian agencies. Classed as a wireless communications equipment manufacturer. Sites include Aberdeen Proving Ground (MD) and Melbourne (FL). Runs mixed-signal R&D and IR&D spanning RF systems, FPGA and firmware, software control, and integration and test.

nodes.name: Jacobs
nodes.description: Engineering, consulting and project delivery firm (NYSE: J). Designs wireless telecommunications systems, including public safety and commercial DAS, neutral host and land mobile radio. Serves national security and defence clients with mission-ready infrastructure and digital systems. Holds a role on the US Missile Defense Agency's SHIELD contract (February 2026).

nodes.name: National Science and Technology Council (NSTC, Taiwan)
nodes.description: Taiwan's cabinet-level science council. Leads the six-year Next-Generation Communications Technology Development Program (2025 to 2030).

nodes.name: Next-Generation Communications Technology Development Program (Taiwan)
nodes.description: Taiwan's national 6G and satellite program, approved by the Cabinet in July 2025: NT$27 billion over six years (2025 to 2030), led by NSTC. Aims for commercial 6G by 2030, satellite ground equipment, experimental and 6G simulation networks, and at least three satellite service providers in Taiwan by 2030.

nodes.name: Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI)
nodes.description: Taiwan's main applied research institute. Its Information and Communications Research Laboratories (ICL) run the 6G-FORMOSA initiative. Signed a 6G MoU with the EU's 6G-SANDBOX (2023) and MoUs with 6G-SENSES and TNO (2025) on sensing and RIS. Co-hosted a UK-Taiwan 6G workshop with the UK telecoms hubs (2025).

nodes.name: 6G-FORMOSA (ITRI)
nodes.description: ITRI's 6G initiative covering AI-RAN, chip development and end-to-end testbeds, with a 6G trial network at its Hsinchu campus as a hub for international collaboration. Work spans non-terrestrial networks, integrated sensing and communication, and RIS.

nodes.name: Chunghwa Telecom
nodes.description: Taiwan's largest operator. Runs a multi-orbit satellite strategy (ST-2 GEO, OneWeb LEO, SES MEO and a dedicated Astranis MicroGEO satellite) and was first in Taiwan licensed for commercial OneWeb LEO services. Its chairman heads the national 6G and satellite alliance.

nodes.name: Taiwan 6G and satellite communications alliance
nodes.description: Alliance of more than 50 Taiwanese companies formed in December 2025 under the national NT$27 billion plan, announced by the Taipei Computer Association. Headed by Chunghwa Telecom's chairman. Prioritises locally developed satellite equipment and user terminals.

nodes.name: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University (NYCU)
nodes.description: Hsinchu university. Vice President Ta-Sung Lee's team works on wide-area 3D networking for B5G and 6G. Home of free5GC, an open-source 5G core extended to 6G.

nodes.name: National Taiwan University (NTU)
nodes.description: Leading Taiwanese university. Runs national 6G projects including key technologies for next-generation communications and sub-THz beamforming. Executive Vice President Wanjiun Liao's team works on user-experience-driven 6G for immersive XR.

nodes.name: National Taiwan University of Science and Technology (Taiwan Tech)
nodes.description: Its Wireless Communication and Electromagnetic Compatibility Research Center works with industry on 6G testing, and with Chunghwa Telecom Laboratories on antenna validation. Part of ITRI's 6G delegation to Europe (2025).

nodes.name: National Tsing Hua University (NTHU)
nodes.description: Hsinchu university. Part of ITRI's 6G delegation to Europe (2025).

nodes.name: National Chung Cheng University (CCU)
nodes.description: Chiayi university. Part of ITRI's 6G delegation to Europe (2025).

nodes.name: Ministry of Digital Affairs (MODA, Taiwan)
nodes.description: Taiwan's spectrum planner. Preparing a 6G spectrum plan by the end of 2026. The 700, 900 and 1800 MHz licences expire at the end of December 2030 and will be re-auctioned for 6G.

nodes.name: TSMC
nodes.description: World's largest contract chipmaker and anchor of Taiwan's semiconductor supply chain.

nodes.name: Compal Electronics
nodes.description: Taiwanese electronics maker in the Open RAN and private 5G market. Supplied white-box O-RAN base stations to NYCU's open-source core team. Part of ITRI's 6G delegation to Europe (2025).

nodes.name: Pegatron
nodes.description: Taiwanese contract manufacturer moving into 5G and Open RAN base stations through its Pegatron 5G unit.

nodes.name: Quanta Cloud Technology (QCT)
nodes.description: Quanta Computer's cloud unit. Supplies 5G RAN and Taiwan's domestic 5G standalone core. Verified multi-vendor O-RAN with Chunghwa Telecom in a national project (2022).

nodes.name: Alpha Networks
nodes.description: Taiwanese networking equipment maker targeting private 5G and Open RAN through its Transnet subsidiary.

nodes.name: TMYTEK (TMY Technology)
nodes.address: No. 3 Yuandong Road, Banqiao, New Taipei City
nodes.description: Taiwanese mmWave company making beamformers, antenna-in-package modules, OTA test systems and RIS for 5G and 6G research. Partnered with Metanoia on FR2 base stations (2026).

nodes.name: Auden Techno
nodes.description: Taiwanese RF and antenna company (TWSE 3138). Makes satellite user terminals, O-RAN high-power radio units and a small RIS for FR2 and FR3.

nodes.name: Metanoia Communications
nodes.description: Taiwanese chip company making software-defined radio chipsets for base stations, including the ALBIZIA FR2 platform.

nodes.name: YTTEK Technology
nodes.description: Taiwanese company developing liquid-crystal reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (LC-RIS) for low-power 6G.

nodes.name: Pang-An Ting
nodes.role: Vice President, ITRI; General Director, Information and Communications Research Laboratories
nodes.description: Leads ITRI's communications research, including 6G-FORMOSA and its links with Europe's 6G-SANDBOX.

nodes.name: Chien Chih-cheng (Alex Chien)
nodes.description: Heads Taiwan's 50-plus-company 6G and satellite alliance.

nodes.name: Lin Faa-jeng
nodes.description: Speaks for the national 6G and satellite program.

nodes.name: Ta-Sung Lee
nodes.description: Leads work on high-speed, wide-area 3D networking for B5G and 6G.

nodes.name: Wanjiun Liao
nodes.role: Executive Vice President and Chair Professor, NTU
nodes.description: Leads user-experience-driven 6G network research for immersive XR.

nodes.name: Hung-Yu Wei
nodes.role: Professor, Department of Electrical Engineering, NTU
nodes.description: Researches edge computing, fog computing and machine learning for networks.

nodes.name: Chang-Fa Yang
nodes.role: Distinguished Professor and Vice President for Industry-Academia Collaboration, Taiwan Tech; Director, Wireless Communication and EMC Research Center
nodes.description: Leads Taiwan Tech's 6G testing work with industry.

nodes.name: Tseng Wen-fang
nodes.role: Director, Department of Resource Management, MODA
nodes.description: Leads Taiwan's 6G spectrum planning.

nodes.name: In-Q-Tel (IQT)
nodes.description: Not-for-profit strategic investor funded mainly by the CIA. Invests in early-stage dual-use technology for the US intelligence and national security community, including satellite communications (an early OneWeb investor), GPS signal processing and space systems.

nodes.name: Telcom Ventures
nodes.description: Private equity and venture firm founded by Rajendra and Neera Singh that invests in telecoms and wireless. Linked holdings include NextNav and Omnispace.

nodes.name: Booz Allen Ventures
nodes.description: Booz Allen Hamilton's corporate venture arm, launched in 2022 with $100 million and tripled to $300 million in 2025. Invests in early-stage companies with federal applications.

nodes.name: RTX Ventures
nodes.description: RTX's corporate venture arm, active in early-stage defence technology rounds.

nodes.name: Lockheed Martin Ventures
nodes.description: Lockheed Martin's venture fund (from 2007), raised from $400 million to $1 billion in April 2026. Next-generation communications is one of its focus areas. Early investor in DeepSig.

nodes.name: Washington Harbour Partners
nodes.description: Investor in mission-critical dual-use and national security businesses, focused on cybersecurity, government and enterprise technology, with growing defence tech activity (Raft, Striveworks, Trusted Space).

nodes.name: VIPC and Virginia Venture Partners
nodes.description: Virginia Innovation Partnership Corporation and its venture program, Virginia Venture Partners (formerly CIT GAP Funds), which invests in early-stage Virginia tech companies. A founding partner of National IQ. The Commonwealth of Virginia is listed among DeepSig's investors.

nodes.name: National Innovation Quarter (National IQ)
nodes.description: Innovation district in National Landing (Crystal City, Pentagon City, Potomac Yard), launched in February 2026. Founding partners include Amazon, Northrop Grumman, SAIC, VIPC, Virginia Tech, and Arlington and Alexandria economic development. Its hub at 1550 Crystal Drive hosts VC in DC, Silicon Valley Defense Group and the Virtus Innovation Center.

nodes.name: VC in DC
nodes.description: Network uniting venture capital across the Mid-Atlantic. Runs vcIQ founder sessions on dual-use and defence tech with National IQ.

nodes.name: Silicon Valley Defense Group
nodes.description: Defence innovation network with a presence at National IQ's Crystal Drive hub; a National IQ sponsor.

nodes.name: Scout Ventures
nodes.description: Early-stage frontier and dual-use technology venture firm. Investor in DeepSig's Series A (2020).

nodes.name: Leawood Venture Capital
nodes.description: Venture firm that led DeepSig's $5 million Series A (2020).

nodes.name: Blu Venture Investors
nodes.description: Mid-Atlantic early-stage investor. Investor in DeepSig's Series A (2020).

nodes.name: Stonemill Ventures
nodes.description: Venture firm listed as a participant in DeepSig's Series A (2020).

nodes.name: American Tower
nodes.description: Tower company. Co-led Federated Wireless's Series B (2017) and joined its Series C (2019).

nodes.name: SBA Communications
nodes.description: Tower company. New investor in Federated Wireless's $51 million Series C (2019).

nodes.name: Charter Communications
nodes.description: US cable operator. Co-led Federated Wireless's $42 million Series B (2017).

nodes.name: Allied Minds
nodes.description: Commercialisation firm that founded Federated Wireless in 2012 to exploit Virginia Tech research, and invested in its Series A to C.

nodes.name: GIC (Singapore sovereign wealth fund)
nodes.description: Singapore's sovereign wealth fund. Investor in Federated Wireless's Series B and C.

nodes.name: Public Wireless Supply Chain Innovation Fund (NTIA)
nodes.description: NTIA grant fund from the CHIPS and Science Act, originally $1.5 billion for open and interoperable wireless networks (Open RAN). The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (July 2025) rescinded $850m of unallocated money. In 2026 NTIA cancelled awards under its third round and put the last $53m into a fourth round on AI-native RAN. Awarded DeepSig grants in 2023 and 2025.

nodes.name: DARPA
nodes.description: US Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency. Funds early-stage defence research, including wireless and spectrum programs, from Arlington.

nodes.name: AFWERX AFVentures
nodes.address: US Department of the Air Force
nodes.description: Commercial investment arm of AFWERX and the Department of the Air Force. Uses SBIR/STTR and STRATFI/TACFI funding ($3 million to $15 million per STRATFI project) to move dual-use startups from prototype to production.

nodes.name: Rajendra Singh
nodes.description: Wireless pioneer who founded LCC International. Director at NextNav and Omnispace.

nodes.name: Chris Moran
nodes.role: Vice President and General Manager, Lockheed Martin Ventures
nodes.description: Leads Lockheed Martin's venture fund.

nodes.name: Mina Faltas
nodes.role: Founder and Chief Investment Officer, Washington Harbour Partners
nodes.description: Sits on boards including Raft and Epirus.

nodes.name: Tom Weithman
nodes.role: Chief Investment Officer, VIPC; Managing Director, Virginia Venture Partners
nodes.description: Leads VIPC's investment programs.

nodes.name: Cyber Bytes Foundation
nodes.description: Non-profit running the Quantico Cyber Hub and the American Cyber League Innovation & Technology Cyber Labs in Stafford County's Quantico HUBZone (opened 2021). The hub hosts Insight Public Sector's vendor-agnostic 5G lab for federal and DoD clients to build and stress-test private LTE, 5G and CBRS. Has hosted Marine Corps research agreements with local firms.

nodes.name: Cesar Nader
nodes.role: Founder and Executive Director, Cyber Bytes Foundation
nodes.description: Founded the Cyber Bytes Foundation and its Quantico technology labs.

nodes.name: Tyrell Junius
nodes.role: Co-Founder and Chief Operating Officer, Tiami Networks
nodes.description: Co-founded Tiami Networks in 2022, which builds secure 5G systems for dual-use applications. Former US Peace Corps Volunteer in Zambia, with international business experience across Africa, Japan, the US and Europe. Speaker at FedInsider's NextGen Cellular Networks event.

nodes.name: Solutional
nodes.description: Consulting firm providing fractional CTO, technology consulting, training and go-to-market services in next-generation networking, network automation and AI. Has worked with Nokia and The Futurum Group on AI and data centre networking.

nodes.name: Scott Robohn
nodes.description: Network operations veteran (Juniper, Cisco, Nokia, DriveNets). Co-founder of the Network Automation Forum (AutoCon), creator and host of the Total Network Operations (TNOps) podcast, and leader of the Virginia Network User Group. Speaker at FedInsider's NextGen Cellular Networks event.

nodes.name: General Services Administration (GSA)
nodes.description: US federal procurement agency. Its Information Technology Category runs the Enterprise Infrastructure Solutions (EIS) contract and the Wireless Mobility Solutions schedule, through which agencies buy 5G services. Published federal guidance on buying secure 5G (2023) under the National Strategy to Secure 5G, and hosts the 200+ member Federal Mobility Group.

nodes.name: Brian Vu
nodes.role: Technical Program Manager, General Services Administration
nodes.description: Works in GSA's Information Technology Category (Federal Acquisition Service), providing solutions engineering for federal agencies on the Enterprise Infrastructure Solutions (EIS) program, managed networking and cybersecurity. Speaker at FedInsider's NextGen Cellular Networks event.

nodes.name: Anthony Lawson
nodes.description: Enterprise networking leader with over 25 years across wired and Wi-Fi infrastructure, 5G cellular, Secure Access Service Edge (SASE) and AI-driven network management. Speaker at FedInsider's NextGen Cellular Networks event.

nodes.name: Capability Program Executive Aviation, U.S. Army (CPE Aviation)
nodes.description: US Army acquisition organisation for aviation programs (formerly PEO Aviation), within ASA(ALT). Has a Chief Digital Transformation Officer under the Army acquisition CDTO program, which drives data-centric changes to processes, technology and culture.

nodes.name: CW4 Reginald Oliver
nodes.role: Chief Digital Transformation Officer, Capability Program Executive Aviation, U.S. Army
nodes.description: Army aviation maintenance officer and AH-64 Maintenance Test Pilot (Warrant Officer since 2008), with tours in Afghanistan and service in the 82nd and 12th Combat Aviation Brigades. Now leads digital transformation for Army aviation acquisition. Speaker at FedInsider's NextGen Cellular Networks event.

nodes.name: Technology Innovation Institute
nodes.description: Abu Dhabi applied research institute. Funds the KU–TII 6G Chair at Khalifa University, kicked off in April 2024. Co-organises the annual 6G Abu Dhabi Summit with Khalifa University.

nodes.name: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology
nodes.description: Saudi research university. Hosts an annual 6G Summit, now in its fifth year. Strong in non-terrestrial networks and terahertz, including THz links for high-altitude platforms with HBKU.

nodes.name: Hamad Bin Khalifa University
nodes.description: Qatar research university. Published a 2026 analysis with KAUST on terahertz links for high-altitude platform stations in 6G non-terrestrial networks.

nodes.name: Zayed University
nodes.description: UAE university. Signed an MoU with e& UAE and Khalifa University to set up the UAE 6G Innovation Hub and national 5G/6G federated testbeds, built on the IEEE 5G/6G Innovation Testbed.

nodes.name: King Saud University
nodes.description: Saudi university in Riyadh. Hosts the New Emerging Technologies and 5G and Beyond Research Chair in its College of Computer and Information Sciences.

nodes.name: e& UAE (etisalat)
nodes.description: UAE operator. Ran the Middle East's first 6G terahertz pilot with NYU Abu Dhabi in October 2025, reaching 145 Gbps. Co-authored the Golden 6 GHz Band white paper with TDRA, KU and NYUAD. Published a 6G engineering framework with NYUAD and KU in October 2026. Partner in the UAE 6G Innovation Hub.

nodes.name: du (Emirates Integrated Telecommunications)
nodes.description: UAE operator. Launched what it calls the world's first commercial end-to-end upper 6 GHz connectivity, using 350 MHz at 6775–7125 MHz. Six-carrier aggregation with Nokia in September 2026. Ran 6G field trials with Khalifa University.

nodes.name: Telecommunications and Digital Government Regulatory Authority
nodes.description: UAE regulator. Owns the national 6G roadmap. Added upper 6 GHz to the National Frequency Plan for IMT in November 2024. Led the April 2026 launch of the world's first commercial upper 6 GHz network ecosystem at the SAMENA Leaders' Summit. Co-published the Golden 6 GHz Band white paper.

nodes.name: stc group
nodes.description: Saudi operator group. Completed the first 7 GHz (6G-enabling) band trial in the Middle East and North Africa with CST and Nokia in November 2025.

nodes.name: Communications, Space & Technology Commission
nodes.description: Saudi regulator for communications, space and technology. Supported stc's first MENA 7 GHz 6G band trial with Nokia.

nodes.name: Advanced Communications and Electronic Systems Company
nodes.description: Saudi digital infrastructure and neutral-host company with local R&D. Built an O-RAN compliant shareable 5G small cell. Signed a 5G and 6G MoU with Movandi at LEAP 2026 in August 2026.

nodes.name: Movandi
nodes.description: US mmWave RF, RFIC and beamforming company. Partnered with ACES in August 2026 on 5G, future 6G and O-RAN infrastructure in Saudi Arabia and the Middle East.

nodes.name: Ooredoo
nodes.description: Qatari operator group. Signed a letter of intent with CRA and Vodafone Qatar in November 2025 for the Qatar 6G Testbed Platform. Ooredoo Kuwait is pushing 5G-Advanced with 1024QAM and 8x8 MIMO.

nodes.name: Communications Regulatory Authority (Qatar)
nodes.description: Qatar regulator. Launched the Qatar 6G Testbed Platform at MWC25 Doha in November 2025, with Ooredoo Qatar and Vodafone Qatar.

nodes.name: Zain Group
nodes.description: Kuwaiti operator group across the Middle East. Zain Kuwait launched nationwide 5G-Advanced in 2025 and tested six-carrier aggregation in September 2026. No dedicated 6G program found yet.

nodes.name: University of Pretoria
nodes.description: South African university. Its Carl and Emily Fuchs Institute for Microelectronics (CEFIM) runs a sub-terahertz measurement facility up to 300 GHz, described as the only one in Africa, for 6G and radio astronomy.

nodes.name: University of Cape Town
nodes.description: South African university. Runs a 5G/6G digital health testbed. Long-running research partnership with TU Berlin on open 5G testbeds for Africa.

nodes.name: MTN Group
nodes.description: Africa's largest operator by customers. MTN South Africa ran what it calls Africa's first upper 6 GHz 5G-Advanced trial with Huawei in October 2026, peaking at 10.35 Gbps under a temporary ICASA licence. Leads the African Group of Six operator alliance.

nodes.name: Vodacom Group
nodes.description: South African operator group, majority owned by Vodafone. Completed its acquisition of a controlling stake in Safaricom in 2026. Member of the African Group of Six.

nodes.name: Safaricom
nodes.description: Kenya's largest operator, now controlled by Vodacom. Holds about 64% of Kenya's mobile broadband market. Runs Kenya's 5G standalone network.

nodes.name: Independent Communications Authority of South Africa
nodes.description: South African regulator. Published its IMT Roadmap 2026 for consultation in July 2026, covering IMT-2030 (6G) spectrum. Its National Radio Frequency Plan 2026 allocates the full 700 MHz upper 6 GHz band to IMT.

nodes.name: Nigerian Communications Commission
nodes.description: Nigerian regulator. Its draft Spectrum Roadmap 2026–2030 earmarks upper 6 GHz for future mobile use and targets about 3.8 GHz of mobile spectrum by 2030.

nodes.name: Communications Authority of Kenya
nodes.description: Kenyan ICT regulator and spectrum manager. Kenya reached 2.1 million 5G subscriptions in June 2026. No published 6G roadmap found yet.

nodes.name: National Telecom Regulatory Authority (Egypt)
nodes.description: Egyptian regulator. Ran Africa's first upper 6 GHz mobile trial with Telecom Egypt and Huawei. Approved the Mobile Spectrum Roadmap 2026–2030 and is preparing a 2030–2035 national spectrum plan.

nodes.name: Telecom Egypt
nodes.description: Egypt's incumbent operator. Ran Africa's first upper 6 GHz mobile trial with NTRA and Huawei.

nodes.name: Samson Lasaulce
nodes.role: Chief Research Scientist; holder of the KU–TII 6G Chair on Native AI
nodes.description: Chief Research Scientist at Khalifa University and holder of the KU–TII 6G Chair on Native AI. Also a CNRS Director of Research in France.

nodes.name: Murat Uysal
nodes.description: Founding Director of the NYU Abu Dhabi Wireless Center. Led the 145 Gbps terahertz pilot with e& UAE in October 2025.

nodes.name: Salman AlQahtani
nodes.role: Dean, College of Computer and Information Sciences, King Saud University
nodes.description: Professor of computer engineering at King Saud University. Dean of its College of Computer and Information Sciences and supervisor of the 5G and Beyond Research Chair. Co-authored a 2021 survey of the 6G ecosystem.

nodes.name: Mohamed-Slim Alouini
nodes.role: Al-Khawarizmi Distinguished Professor of ECE, KAUST
nodes.description: Leads the KAUST Communication Theory Lab and chairs the KAUST 6G Summit. UNESCO Chair on Education to Connect the Unconnected. Elected to the US National Academy of Engineering in February 2026.

nodes.name: Marwan Bin Shaker
nodes.role: Acting Chief Technology and Information Officer, e& UAE
nodes.description: Acting CTIO of e& UAE. Spokesperson for the 145 Gbps terahertz pilot with NYU Abu Dhabi.

nodes.name: Saleem Alblooshi
nodes.description: CTO of du. Led its commercial upper 6 GHz launch.

nodes.name: Tariq Al Awadhi
nodes.description: Leads spectrum affairs at TDRA. Public face of the UAE's upper 6 GHz policy and the Golden 6 GHz Band white paper.

nodes.name: Maryam Rofougaran
nodes.description: CEO and co-founder of Movandi. Signed the 2026 ACES partnership for 5G and 6G in Saudi Arabia.

nodes.name: Tinus Stander
nodes.description: Professor at the University of Pretoria's Carl and Emily Fuchs Institute for Microelectronics. Leads its sub-terahertz measurement facility for 6G research.

nodes.name: Joyce Mwangama
nodes.description: Associate Professor at the University of Cape Town. Built South Africa's first university 5G testbed and now works on AI-run community 5G with TU Berlin.

nodes.name: Angela Wamola
nodes.description: Head of Africa at the GSMA, previously Head of Sub-Saharan Africa. Leads GSMA policy work across the continent.

nodes.name: Ferdi Moolman
nodes.description: CEO of MTN South Africa. Spokesperson for its October 2026 upper 6 GHz 5G-Advanced trial.

nodes.name: Aminu Maida
nodes.role: Executive Vice Chairman and CEO, NCC
nodes.description: Head of the Nigerian Communications Commission. Opened the January 2026 consultation on the Spectrum Roadmap 2026–2030.

nodes.name: Mohamed Shamroukh
nodes.description: Head of Egypt's NTRA. Announced Africa's first upper 6 GHz mobile trial and the 2030–2035 spectrum plan.

nodes.name: Turkcell
nodes.description: Turkish operator. Runs Turkcell 6GEN.LAB, an AI and 6G lab and the country's main 6G research hub. Tested Türkiye's first home-grown reconfigurable intelligent surface prototypes with TÜBİTAK in October 2026, and field-tested 6G sensing (ISAC) in Istanbul. Signed 6G MoUs with Ericsson in 2024 and 2026. Partner in six European R&D projects including MAGIC-6G.

nodes.name: Türk Telekom
nodes.description: Turkish incumbent operator. Runs 6G R&D and Innovation Laboratories in Ankara, with outdoor pilots planned around ODTÜ Teknokent in summer 2026. Works with Ericsson Research Türkiye on SafeRoute-6G and 6G standards. Set up an R&D and Innovation Science Board in September 2026.

nodes.name: TÜBİTAK (Scientific and Technological Research Council of Türkiye)
nodes.description: Türkiye's national research council and main research funder. Its MAM and BİLGEM institutes built the first domestic intelligent-surface prototypes for 6G with Turkcell in 2026.

nodes.name: TÜBİTAK BİLGEM
nodes.description: TÜBİTAK's informatics and information security research centre. Its HİSAR Lab co-developed Türkiye's first domestic SRS, STS and RIS designs for 6G with Turkcell 6GEN.LAB.

nodes.name: TÜBİTAK Marmara Research Center
nodes.description: TÜBİTAK research centre at Gebze. Its MİLTAL / Functional Materials team co-developed the 2026 intelligent-surface prototypes for 6G with Turkcell. Hosted part of the field tests.

nodes.name: ULAK Communications (ULAK Haberleşme)
nodes.description: Turkish base station maker, majority owned by ASELSAN (51%) with HAVELSAN (25%). Has filed 208 6G patent applications, covering non-terrestrial networks, AI/ML, ISAC, beamforming and cell-free systems. Runs a TÜBİTAK-backed 6G research lab.

nodes.name: ASELSAN
nodes.description: Turkish defence electronics group. Majority shareholder in ULAK and a board member of the HABTEK 6G cluster.

nodes.name: Information and Communication Technologies Authority (BTK)
nodes.description: Turkish telecoms regulator. Published a 6G mobile communication technologies report in March 2025. Runs a 5G and Beyond Joint Graduate Support Program with METU, Bilkent and Hacettepe, and the 5G Valley open test field.

nodes.name: HABTEK (6G and Beyond Communication Technologies Cluster)
nodes.description: Turkish 6G cluster launched in February 2026 at Istanbul Medipol University, backed by the Ministry of Industry and Technology. Members include ASELSAN, Turkcell, TÜBİTAK BİLGEM, ULAK, Vestel and Netaş.

nodes.name: Istanbul Medipol University
nodes.description: Istanbul university. Hosts the HABTEK 6G cluster. Its CoSiNC group, led by Hüseyin Arslan, is a full member of the 6G-IA.

nodes.name: Bilkent University
nodes.description: Ankara university. Partner in BTK's 5G and Beyond Joint Graduate Support Program and the 5G Valley open test field.

nodes.name: Middle East Technical University (ODTÜ)
nodes.description: Ankara university. Partner in BTK's 5G and Beyond graduate program and 5G Valley. Türk Telekom planned its first outdoor 6G pilots around ODTÜ Teknokent in summer 2026.

nodes.name: Israel Innovation Authority
nodes.description: Israel's innovation funding agency. Launched the IISAC consortium in February 2025 as part of a NIS 100m (about $28m) package, to develop sensing, 4D positioning and network efficiency for Beyond 5G/6G.

nodes.name: IISAC Consortium (Intelligent Integrated Sensing and Communication)
nodes.description: Israel Innovation Authority consortium announced in February 2025. Brings Israeli companies and universities together on integrated sensing and communication for Beyond 5G/6G.

nodes.name: Technion – Israel Institute of Technology
nodes.description: Israel's leading engineering university. Home to Shlomo Shamai, a leading information theorist working on cloud radio networks and NOMA.

nodes.name: Weizmann Institute of Science
nodes.description: Israeli research institute. Yonina Eldar's group works on 6G ISAC, near-field communications and dynamic metasurface antennas.

nodes.name: Tel Aviv University
nodes.description: Israeli university. Its engineering faculty works on 5G/6G, mmWave and terahertz links, and satellite communications. Setting up an Institute for Electromagnetic Technologies around the national NEW-ARC wireless research centre.

nodes.name: Gilat Satellite Networks
nodes.description: Israeli satellite ground-segment company. Demonstrated 3GPP-compliant 5G NTN over GEO in February 2026, a step towards satellite-integrated 6G.

nodes.name: Ceragon Networks
nodes.description: Israeli wireless backhaul company. Publishes work on transport planning for 5G-Advanced and early 6G, including E-band.

nodes.name: RunEL NGMT
nodes.description: Israeli 5G RAN start-up specialising in PHY/MAC and O-RAN radio units. Took part in the EU 6G BRAINS project. Now focused on centimetre-level positioning with Amarisoft.

nodes.name: Ucom
nodes.description: Armenian operator. Signed an MoU with Nokia in October 2025 on autonomous networks and AI for 6G, including lab or field trials and 3GPP input.

nodes.name: Telecom Armenia (Team Telecom Armenia)
nodes.description: Armenian incumbent operator. Signed a reciprocal internet transit deal with AzerTelecom in June 2026, a first between Armenia and Azerbaijan.

nodes.name: AzerTelecom
nodes.description: Azerbaijani wholesale operator, part of NEQSOL Holding. Runs the Digital Silk Way project. Signed a reciprocal internet transit deal with Telecom Armenia in June 2026.

nodes.name: Digital Silk Way
nodes.description: AzerTelecom-led fibre corridor linking Europe to Central and South Asia through Georgia, Azerbaijan and the Caspian. Includes the Trans-Caspian cable with Kazakhtelecom. Backbone, not 6G radio.

nodes.name: Regional Commonwealth in the Field of Communications (RCC)
nodes.description: Regional telecoms body for Russia and Central Asian administrations. Coordinates a common position for WRC-27, including the IMT bands under agenda item 1.7.

nodes.name: Kazakhtelecom
nodes.description: Kazakhstan's incumbent operator. Owns 51% of Kcell and sold Tele2/Altel to Qatar's PIH in January 2025. Partner in the Trans-Caspian fibre link of the Digital Silk Way.

nodes.name: Kcell
nodes.description: Kazakh mobile operator, 51% owned by Kazakhtelecom. Rated fastest network in Kazakhstan, including on 5G, in 2026. No published 6G program found.

nodes.name: Beeline Kazakhstan (KaR-Tel)
nodes.description: Kazakh mobile operator. Shares rural network infrastructure with Kcell and Tele2. Leads on coverage. No published 6G program found.

nodes.name: Uztelecom
nodes.description: Uzbekistan's national operator. Demonstrated upper 6 GHz 5G-Advanced at 10.16 Gbit/s at ICT Week 2025, pitched as 6G-ready infrastructure.

nodes.name: Ucell
nodes.description: Uzbek mobile operator. Rated fastest mobile network in Uzbekistan for the third year in 2026. Launched 5G FWA with Huawei. No published 6G program found.

nodes.name: Ministry of Digital Technologies (Uzbekistan)
nodes.description: Uzbek ministry. Signed an MoU with ZTE in April 2026 covering data centres, broadband and next-generation technologies including 6G.

nodes.name: Nazarbayev University
nodes.description: Kazakhstan's research university. Its ECE department runs 6G work on reconfigurable intelligent surfaces and fluid antennas. Plans a 6G research centre.

nodes.name: Tashkent University of Information Technologies
nodes.description: Uzbekistan's main ICT university. Partners with ZTE on hackathons, internships and training.

nodes.name: Orhan Aydın
nodes.description: President of TÜBİTAK since 14 September 2024. Champions its 6G work with Turkcell.

nodes.name: Güneş Fatma Kesik
nodes.role: Manager, Turkcell 6GEN.LAB; Associate Director, Next Generation R&D
nodes.description: Leads Turkcell 6GEN.LAB. Joined Turkcell in 2025 from Ericsson, where she managed research and innovation engagements. Co-author on 6G and AI-native networking.

nodes.name: Vehbi Çağrı Güngör
nodes.role: Executive Vice President, Network Technologies, Turkcell
nodes.description: Turkcell executive responsible for network technologies. Previously CTO. Signed the 2024 Ericsson 6G MoU.

nodes.name: Ebubekir Şahin
nodes.description: CEO of Türk Telekom. Signed the 2026 Ericsson 6G standards collaboration.

nodes.name: Ruşen Kömürcü
nodes.description: Head of ULAK. Has driven its 6G patent push to 208 applications.

nodes.name: Ali Görçin
nodes.description: Head of TÜBİTAK BİLGEM and a HABTEK board member.

nodes.name: Hüseyin Arslan
nodes.role: Dean, School of Engineering and Natural Sciences, Istanbul Medipol University
nodes.description: Dean at Medipol and leader of the CoSiNC research group, a 6G-IA member. Driving force behind HABTEK.

nodes.name: Mehmet Oğul
nodes.description: General Manager of Ericsson Türkiye. Spokesperson for the 2026 Türk Telekom 6G collaboration.

nodes.name: Shlomo Shamai
nodes.role: Technion Distinguished Professor; William Fondiller Chair of Telecommunications
nodes.description: Technion Distinguished Professor. Shannon Award winner. Works on cloud and fog radio networks, NOMA and modern coding.

nodes.name: Yonina Eldar
nodes.role: Professor, Mathematics and Computer Science, Weizmann Institute
nodes.description: Weizmann professor whose group leads work on 6G ISAC, near-field beam focusing and metasurface antennas.

nodes.name: Zion Hadad
nodes.description: Founder and CEO of RunEL, an Israeli 5G RAN company.

nodes.name: Adi Sfadia
nodes.description: CEO of Gilat. Leading its push into multi-orbit and 5G NTN ground segment.

nodes.name: Ralph Yirikian
nodes.description: Head of Ucom. Signed the 2025 6G MoU with Nokia.

nodes.name: Alexander Yesayan
nodes.role: Co-founder and Chairman of the Board, Team Telecom Armenia
nodes.description: Co-founder and chair of Team Telecom Armenia. Public face of the 2026 AzerTelecom transit deal.

nodes.name: Galymzhan Nauryzbayev
nodes.description: Leads Kazakhstan's main 6G research on RIS and fluid antennas. Plans a 6G research centre.

nodes.name: Askar Zhambakin
nodes.role: Chairman of the Management Board, Kcell
nodes.description: Head of Kcell.

nodes.name: Andrey Shishkovsky
nodes.description: CEO of Ucell.

nodes.name: Telia
nodes.description: Nordic and Baltic operator group headquartered in Sweden. Signed the 'Ericsson and Telia Collaborate on 6G in Sweden' MoU on 2 November 2026 (#6GSweden). At the Stockholm launch the partners showed pre-standard 6G over the air in the upper 6 GHz band, and an ISAC demo in which modified 5G radios detected and tracked multiple drones, giving live location, velocity and elevation. Plans 6G trials and may use Digital Arena Sweden as a test environment.

nodes.name: Patrik Hofbauer
nodes.description: President and CEO of Telia. Launched the #6GSweden collaboration with Ericsson in November 2026.

nodes.name: Anders Olsson
nodes.description: Head of Telia Sweden. Attended the November 2026 launch of the Ericsson-Telia 6G collaboration.

nodes.name: Per Narvinger
nodes.description: President and CEO of Ericsson since 1 October 2026, succeeding Börje Ekholm. Joined Ericsson in 1997 and previously led Business Area Networks and Cloud Software and Services. Launched the #6GSweden collaboration with Telia in November 2026.

nodes.name: Patrick Johansson
nodes.role: Head of Europe, Middle East and Africa, Ericsson
nodes.description: Head of Europe, Middle East and Africa at Ericsson. Attended the November 2026 launch of the Ericsson-Telia 6G collaboration.

nodes.name: Natasha Sayce-Zelem
nodes.role: Group Director of AI Product, BT Group
nodes.description: Group Director of AI Product at BT Group since November 2026, working across BT, EE and Plusnet. Her remit runs from critical national infrastructure and sovereign AI to customer experience. Previously Director of Digital and Business Platforms at Lloyds Banking Group, and before that at Amazon Prime and Sky.

nodes.name: AI-RAN Alliance
nodes.description: Global alliance founded at MWC 2024 by Ericsson, Nokia, Samsung, Microsoft, T-Mobile and others to build AI into the radio access network. Reached 132 members in February 2026 and added Qualcomm, SK Telecom and Vodafone to its board. Chaired by Alex Jinsung Choi (SoftBank).

nodes.name: Arm
nodes.description: UK chip architecture company. Sits on the AI-RAN Alliance board.

nodes.name: Justin Hotard
nodes.description: President and CEO of Nokia since 1 April 2025, after leading Intel's Data Center and AI Group. Has refocused Nokia on AI-native networks and agreed a strategic partnership with NVIDIA, including a $1bn NVIDIA investment, to speed AI-RAN and the move to 6G.

nodes.name: Mathias Riback
nodes.role: VP & Head of Advanced Technology U.S., Ericsson; Treasurer, AI-RAN Alliance
nodes.description: Heads Ericsson's Advanced Technology U.S. team, representing the global CTO office in Silicon Valley. Treasurer of the AI-RAN Alliance.

nodes.name: Tae Moon (TM) Roh
nodes.role: Co-CEO and Head of Device eXperience (DX), Samsung Electronics
nodes.description: Co-CEO of Samsung Electronics since November 2025 and head of its Device eXperience division, including the mobile business.

nodes.name: Young Hyun Jun
nodes.role: Vice Chairman, Co-CEO and Head of Device Solutions (DS), Samsung Electronics
nodes.description: Vice Chairman and co-CEO of Samsung Electronics. Leads the Device Solutions (semiconductor) division and the memory business.

nodes.name: Cristiano Amon
nodes.description: CEO of Qualcomm. Used his MWC 2026 keynote to argue that 6G will be critical for AI workloads and agents, and will lift performance in existing spectrum by 50 to 70%.

nodes.name: John Kuzin
nodes.role: SVP, Spectrum Policy & Regulatory Counsel, Qualcomm
nodes.description: Leads Qualcomm's worldwide spectrum policy, including its 6G spectrum advocacy before the FCC and other regulators.

nodes.name: Jensen Huang
nodes.description: Founder and CEO of NVIDIA. Has positioned NVIDIA as a compute platform for AI-RAN and AI-native 6G, including its October 2025 $1bn investment in Nokia.

nodes.name: Ren Zhengfei
nodes.description: Founder of Huawei (1987) and its CEO since 1988.

nodes.name: Yoshiaki Maeda
nodes.description: President and CEO of NTT DOCOMO.

nodes.name: Yongguang Zhang
nodes.description: Microsoft researcher who led Open RAN R&D in Azure for Operators (2020 to 2024) and now leads Microsoft's AI-RAN thinking. IEEE Fellow for software radio.

nodes.name: Mo Jabbari
nodes.role: Director of Telco and Networking Solutions, Arm; Director, AI-RAN Alliance
nodes.description: Arm's director of telco and networking solutions. Sits on the AI-RAN Alliance board.

nodes.name: Rob Soni
nodes.role: VP, RAN Technology, AT&T; Chair, Next G Alliance Full Member Group
nodes.description: Leads AT&T's RAN architecture and technology roadmaps. Chairs the Next G Alliance Full Member Group and the Telecom Infra Project.

nodes.name: Havish Koorapaty
nodes.role: Ericsson; Co-Chair, Next G Alliance Steering Group
nodes.description: Ericsson representative and co-chair of the Next G Alliance Steering Group.

nodes.name: Mark Cudak
nodes.role: Nokia; Chair, Next G Alliance Spectrum Working Group
nodes.description: Nokia researcher who chairs the Next G Alliance Spectrum Working Group.

nodes.name: Alexander Sayenko
nodes.role: Apple; Vice Chair, Next G Alliance Spectrum Working Group
nodes.description: Apple representative and vice chair of the Next G Alliance Spectrum Working Group.

nodes.name: Lola Awoniyi-Oteri
nodes.role: Qualcomm; Vice Chair, Next G Alliance Market & Applications Working Group
nodes.description: Qualcomm representative and vice chair of the Next G Alliance Market & Applications Working Group.

nodes.name: Colin Willcock
nodes.role: Nokia; Chairperson, 6G-IA; Chair, SNS JU Governing Board
nodes.description: Re-elected Chairperson of the 6G-IA in 2026 for a three-year term. Also chairs the SNS JU Governing Board.

nodes.name: Raffaele de Peppe
nodes.description: TIM representative, re-elected Vice-Chairperson of the 6G-IA in 2026.

nodes.name: Afif Osseiran
nodes.description: Ericsson representative, re-elected Treasurer of the 6G-IA in 2026. Also a 6G-IA representative on the SNS JU Governing Board.

nodes.name: Alexandros Kaloxylos
nodes.description: Executive Director of the 6G Smart Networks and Services Industry Association.

nodes.name: Kostas Trichias
nodes.description: Coordinates 6G research and innovation for the 6G-IA office.

nodes.name: Milos Tesanovic
nodes.role: Head of Communication Standards, Samsung R&D Institute UK; 6G-IA Governing Board
nodes.description: Leads communication standards at Samsung R&D Institute UK. Elected to the 6G-IA Governing Board in March 2026 for three years.

nodes.name: Marie-Hélène Hamon
nodes.description: Orange representative on the 6G-IA Governing Board (2026 to 2029).

nodes.name: Petr Ledl
nodes.description: Deutsche Telekom representative on the 6G-IA Governing Board (2026 to 2029).

nodes.name: Javier Garcia Rodrigo
nodes.description: Telefónica representative on the 6G-IA Governing Board (2026 to 2029) and on the SNS JU Governing Board.

nodes.name: Atle Monrad
nodes.description: InterDigital standards lead. Re-elected chair of 3GPP SA6 (application enablement) for a second term in February 2026.

nodes.name: Pivotal Commware
nodes.description: mmWave repeater and antenna company built on Holographic Beam Forming, a software-defined metamaterials antenna. Spun out of Intellectual Ventures in 2016. Backed by Bill Gates; its $102m Series D was led by Gates Frontier and Tracker Capital.

nodes.name: Kymeta
nodes.description: Flat-panel, electronically steered metamaterial satellite terminal maker and an Intellectual Ventures spin-out. Building multi-band (Ku/Ka), multi-orbit terminals for defence and enterprise, with prototypes from mid-2026 and commercial availability planned for 2027.

nodes.name: Echodyne
nodes.description: Radar maker using metamaterials electronically scanned array (MESA) technology, an Intellectual Ventures spin-out. Supplies counter-drone radars to US and allied forces. Opened a plant in July 2026 able to build more than 30,000 radars a year.

nodes.name: ZaiNar
nodes.description: Turns existing 5G and Wi-Fi networks into sub-metre positioning and timing systems without new hardware. Emerged from nine years in stealth in February 2026 with more than $100m raised at a valuation above $1bn.

nodes.name: Elveo Mobile (Lynk Global and Omnispace)
nodes.description: Direct-to-device satellite operator formed when Lynk Global and Omnispace completed their merger on 14 August 2026. Combines Lynk's LEO smallsat technology with Omnispace's 60 MHz of global S-band spectrum. SES is a strategic shareholder. Plans 320 LEO satellites, with services from early 2028.

nodes.name: Hubble Network
nodes.description: Satellite network that connects standard Bluetooth Low Energy chips directly to LEO satellites for low-power IoT. Raised a $200m Series C in September 2026 at a $1.6bn valuation and opened the network to any Bluetooth device. Plans to grow from six to 60 satellites.

nodes.name: Eben Frankenberg
nodes.description: CEO of Echodyne, scaling MESA radar production for counter-drone defence.

nodes.name: Daniel Jacker
nodes.description: Co-founder and CEO of ZaiNar.

nodes.name: Ramu Potarazu
nodes.description: CEO of Elveo Mobile and previously CEO of Lynk Global.

nodes.name: Alex Haro
nodes.description: Co-founder and CEO of Hubble Network.

nodes.name: Pardeep Kohli
nodes.description: President and CEO of Mavenir. Led its 2025 recapitalisation and its move away from radio hardware towards AI-native software.

nodes.name: TERASi
nodes.description: KTH spin-out building compact, hard-to-detect and hard-to-jam millimetre-wave data links using MEMS technology, for defence and satellite communications. Raised an €11m seed round in September 2026, co-led by the NATO Innovation Fund (its first direct investment in Sweden) and JOIN Capital.

nodes.name: NATO Innovation Fund (NIF)
nodes.description: €1bn multi-sovereign venture fund backed by 24 NATO countries, investing in deep tech for defence, security and resilience. Co-led TERASi's €11m seed round in September 2026.

nodes.name: JOIN Capital
nodes.description: Early-stage European deep-tech venture fund. Co-led TERASi's €11m seed round with the NATO Innovation Fund.

nodes.name: D3 (Dare to Defend Democracy)
nodes.description: Kyiv-based early-stage venture fund, founded in 2023, investing in defence and deep tech for Ukraine and its NATO allies, including drones, electronic warfare, sensors and AI. Joined TERASi's seed round in 2026.

nodes.name: Navigare Ventures
nodes.description: Swedish early-stage investor. Backed TERASi at pre-seed and returned for its 2026 seed round.

nodes.name: Almi Invest
nodes.description: Swedish state-backed venture investor. Returning investor in TERASi's 2026 seed round.

nodes.name: Cisco Investments
nodes.description: Cisco's corporate venture arm. Co-led ODC's $45m Series A in March 2026.

nodes.name: Cerberus Capital Management
nodes.description: Private investment firm. Its affiliates made the seed investment in ODC, which calls itself a Cerberus portfolio company.

nodes.name: Intel Capital
nodes.description: Intel's corporate venture arm, investing in silicon, 5G, devices and cloud. Intel dropped its 2025 plan to spin it out. It now stays in-house and is more selective about new deals.

nodes.name: Qualcomm Ventures
nodes.description: Qualcomm's global investment arm. In 2026 it announced a strategic AI venture fund of up to $150m for Indian startups.

nodes.name: Samsung NEXT Ventures
nodes.description: Investment arm of Samsung NEXT, an innovation group within Samsung Electronics. Mostly invests in early-stage software and AI.

nodes.name: Verizon Ventures
nodes.description: Verizon's corporate venture arm. It has reportedly stopped making new investments and now manages its existing portfolio of around 42 companies, which includes Pivotal Commware.

nodes.name: T-Mobile Ventures
nodes.description: T-Mobile's corporate venture fund for 5G, industrial and IoT products. Its second fund launched in 2023 and is managed with Touchdown Ventures.

nodes.name: Wayra (Telefónica)
nodes.description: Telefónica's corporate venture capital arm and open innovation platform. It now also covers the work Telefónica Ventures used to do.

nodes.name: DTCP (Digital Transformation Capital Partners)
nodes.description: Investment firm founded as Deutsche Telekom Capital Partners. Now independent, with Deutsche Telekom as anchor investor. Its new defence fund reached a €455m first close in September 2026.

nodes.name: NTT DOCOMO Ventures
nodes.description: NTT DOCOMO group's corporate venture arm. Manages DOCOMO Innovation Fund IV (¥15bn, launched January 2026).

nodes.name: Intellectual Ventures
nodes.description: Invention and patent business that spun out metamaterials companies including Kymeta, Echodyne and Pivotal Commware. Bill Gates invested in each.

nodes.name: 6G-VERSUS (6G Vertical Trials for Sustainability)
nodes.description: SNS JU-funded Horizon Europe project (2025 to 2027), coordinated by the University of Oulu. Runs 6G vertical trials for sustainability, plus a venture accelerator for 25 EU startups and SMEs (September to November 2026).

nodes.name: IITP (Institute for Information & Communications Technology Planning & Evaluation)
nodes.description: R&D management agency under Korea's MSIT. It funds about ₩1.9 trillion of AI and ICT projects in 2026, plus a national 6G demonstration planned for 2028.

nodes.name: UK Telecoms Innovation Network (UKTIN)
nodes.description: DSIT-funded network that helps UK telecoms firms find R&D funding, testbeds and partners. It is delivered with Digital Catapult, Cambridge Wireless, the University of Bristol and WM5G, and continued from April 2025.

nodes.name: Platforms for Advanced Wireless Research (PAWR)
nodes.description: NSF program that runs city-scale wireless testbeds for 5G, 6G and beyond: POWDER (Salt Lake City), COSMOS (New York City), AERPAW (Research Triangle, NC) and the rural ARA testbed, plus the Colosseum emulator. Its Project Office is co-led by US Ignite and Northeastern University. All the platforms are O-RAN Alliance Open Testing and Integration Centres (OTICs).

nodes.name: POWDER
nodes.description: PAWR city-scale wireless testbed in Salt Lake City, used for Open RAN testing and validation.

nodes.name: COSMOS
nodes.description: PAWR city-scale wireless testbed in New York City. In 2026 NSF backed an AI-ready testbed project built on it.

nodes.name: AERPAW
nodes.description: PAWR testbed for drone-based wireless systems in the Research Triangle area of North Carolina. It was the last PAWR platform to become an O-RAN OTIC.

nodes.name: Colosseum
nodes.description: The world's largest wireless network emulator, with 256 programmable software radios. Run by Northeastern University at its Burlington innovation campus and used as an Open RAN digital twin. Part of PAWR.

nodes.name: King's College London (Centre for Telecommunications Research)
nodes.description: King's Centre for Telecommunications Research (founded 1994) works on 6G, from mission-critical to AI-native networks. Founding partner in the £12m REASON project and co-founder of 6G Futures with the University of Bristol. Hosted London 6G Week in September 2026.

nodes.name: Seoul National University
nodes.description: Leading Korean university. One of the universities Samsung partnered with in 2021 on next-generation communications talent and research.

nodes.name: 6G-LEADER (Learning-driven and Evolved Radio for 6G)
nodes.description: SNS JU Call 3 project (about €8m EU contribution, 36 months) advancing 6G physical layer and RAN: ML-driven PHY, full-duplex transceivers and open, disaggregated RAN. Has 18 partners, with the University of Cyprus as technical coordinator. Digital Catapult is a partner.

nodes.name: Greenerwave
nodes.description: Paris startup (founded 2015) that shapes electromagnetic waves with reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) and metasurface antennas, for 5G/6G connectivity, ISAC, radar and satellite terminals. Supplies RIS to the SNS JU project SUNRISE-6G. Has a strategic partnership with Telespazio France.

nodes.name: Noema Signal Labs
nodes.description: 2026 spin-out from the University of Surrey's 6G Innovation Centre. Its signal processing lets existing masts carry more data and connect more devices. Won the Best Startup Award at the 2026 EuCNC & 6G Summit, joined Deutsche Telekom's Tangible Tomorrow program (hubraum with T-Labs) and has raised around £1.2m.

nodes.name: aeroLiFi
nodes.description: Wessling (near Munich) company developing LiFi and visible light communication. Works on hybrid LiFi/Wi-Fi/5G/6G links and end-to-end optical networks. Presented to the 6G-IA at the 2024 SNS JU brokerage event.

nodes.name: Astrome
nodes.description: Bengaluru deep-tech company (founded 2015) making E-band millimetre-wave backhaul (GigaMesh), phased-array antennas and satellite communications products. GigaMesh delivers fibre-like wireless backhaul for rural and 5G sites. Previously raised $10m in a round led by Apollo.

nodes.name: HJWAVE
nodes.description: Korean mmWave RF company making 3D waveguide antennas for 24 to 140 GHz. Released Korea's first D-band (140 GHz) antenna for autonomous driving radar and 6G mobile communication.

nodes.name: KREEMO
nodes.description: Seoul antenna company with mmWave antennas, phased-array beamforming and transparent antenna technology, including a 360-degree 5G mmWave stacked patch antenna. Expanding into satellite and defence antennas.

nodes.name: Astrum Mobile
nodes.description: Singapore satellite-to-device (S2D) company building a 3GPP 5G NTN service for ordinary phones across Asia-Pacific from a geostationary satellite, NEASTAR-1, built by SWISSto12. Ran a 5G broadcast trial over a GEO satellite to a retail smartphone with Qualcomm.

nodes.name: Konstantinos Nikitopoulos
nodes.role: Founder, Noema Signal Labs; Professor, University of Surrey 6GIC
nodes.description: Professor of Wireless Communications and Signal Processing at Surrey's 6G Innovation Centre and founder of Noema Signal Labs.

nodes.name: HSE University Telecommunications Research Institute (MIEM)
nodes.description: Telecoms institute at HSE University's Tikhonov Moscow Institute of Electronics and Mathematics (MIEM). Demonstrated a sub-THz 6G link (141 to 164 GHz, 12 Gbps, automatic switching when blocked). Runs the Priority 2030 project "Trusted 6G Communication Systems Technology Suite", a 5G/6G research testbed and terahertz neuromorphic circuit research. Partners with Moscow DIT on 5G and 6G.

nodes.name: Skoltech Project Center for Next Generation Wireless and IoT
nodes.description: Skoltech centre developing 5G solutions, Open RAN, private 5G and hybrid non-terrestrial networks, plus a 6G Technologies Laboratory. In August 2025 it won a Ministry of Digital Development subsidy for critical 5G-Advanced and 6G equipment technologies (three years).

nodes.name: NIC Telecom (National Research Centre for Telecommunications, formerly NIIR)
nodes.description: Russia's state telecoms research centre under the Ministry of Digital Development. Formed from the Radio Research and Development Institute (NIIR) and absorbed ZNIIS; renamed in January 2025. Leads Russian 6G spectrum analysis ahead of WRC-27 and, with Skoltech, the state 6G foundation work.

nodes.name: Ministry of Digital Development, Communications and Mass Media (Russia)
nodes.description: Russian federal ministry for telecoms. Allocated a 750m rouble subsidy for 6G foundation work by Skoltech and NIC Telecom, with first pilot zones planned by 2028. Says a 6G standard may be approved by 2028 to 2030.

nodes.name: Moscow Department of Information Technology (DIT)
nodes.description: Moscow city IT department. Signed a partnership with HSE University to advance 5G and 6G networks.

nodes.name: ICS Holding
nodes.description: Russian technology holding that owns Yadro and Bureau 1440.

nodes.name: Yadro
nodes.description: ICS Holding's server and telecoms hardware maker. Builds domestic base stations (BTS8100). Invested 30bn roubles in base stations from 2022 to 2025 and plans another 30bn in 2026. Supplies MegaFon, Beeline (VimpelCom) and Rostelecom.

nodes.name: Irteya
nodes.description: Russian base station maker. Has a forward contract to supply MTS with about 20,000 base stations by 2030 and also supplies VimpelCom. Expects to ship about 3,000 base stations in 2026. Russian components make up under 5% of its 5G-capable stations, with a 30% target by 2028.

nodes.name: Bulat
nodes.description: Rostelecom subsidiary developing Russian 2G/4G base stations. Rostelecom is folding it into a new equipment holding based on its subsidiary Technowave. Supplies Rostelecom and MegaFon.

nodes.name: Rostelecom
nodes.description: Russia's state-backed national telecoms operator. Owns base station developer Bulat and buys Yadro equipment. Says Russia must free 5G spectrum and settle its domestic-equipment network architecture before 6G work begins.

nodes.name: MTS (Mobile TeleSystems)
nodes.description: Major Russian mobile operator and Irteya's anchor customer, rolling out thousands of domestic base stations. Says 5G spectrum and network architecture must come before 6G.

nodes.name: MegaFon
nodes.description: Major Russian mobile operator. Taking 1,500 Yadro base stations in 2026 and also buys from Bulat.

nodes.name: VimpelCom (Beeline)
nodes.description: Major Russian mobile operator (Beeline brand). Installing Yadro and Irteya base stations. Says 5G spectrum and the move off 2G/3G must come before 6G.

nodes.name: STC PROTEY
nodes.description: St Petersburg developer of mobile core network software. Signed its first export deal in 2025, supplying a network core for base stations in Afghanistan.

nodes.name: Bureau 1440
nodes.description: ICS Holding company building Rassvet, a Russian LEO broadband constellation using 5G NTN and laser inter-satellite links. Launched its first 16 production satellites on 23 March 2026 and a second batch in July 2026. Plans commercial service in 2027 and up to 900 satellites by 2035.

nodes.name: Mobile Research Group
nodes.description: Russian mobile industry analysis group.

nodes.name: Evgeny Koucheryavy
nodes.description: Directs HSE's Telecommunications Research Institute and leads its sub-THz 6G work.

nodes.name: Alexey Frolov
nodes.role: Director, Skoltech Project Center for Next Generation Wireless and IoT
nodes.description: Full professor and director of Skoltech's wireless centre. Head of its 6G Technologies Laboratory.

nodes.name: Evgeny Devyatkin
nodes.role: Director, Centre for Advanced Wireless Communications Research, NIC Telecom
nodes.description: Leads NIC Telecom's advanced wireless research, including Russia's 6G spectrum analysis for WRC-27.

nodes.name: Maksut Shadayev
nodes.description: Russian Minister of Digital Development, Communications and Mass Media.

nodes.name: Alexei Shelobkov
nodes.description: CEO of ICS Holding, parent of Yadro and Bureau 1440.

nodes.name: Dmitry Lakontsev
nodes.description: CEO of base station maker Irteya.

nodes.name: Alexander Loginov
nodes.role: CEO, Bulat and Rostelecom equipment holding
nodes.description: CEO of Bulat and of Rostelecom's new equipment holding. Also a Rostelecom deputy CEO.

nodes.name: Mikhail Oseyevsky
nodes.description: CEO of Rostelecom.

nodes.name: Inessa Galaktionova
nodes.description: CEO of MTS.

nodes.name: Khachatur Pombukhchan
nodes.description: CEO of MegaFon.

nodes.name: Sergey Anokhin
nodes.description: CEO of VimpelCom (Beeline).

nodes.name: Vladimir Freinkman
nodes.description: Vice president of STC PROTEY.

nodes.name: Eldar Murtazin
nodes.description: Russian mobile industry analyst, frequently quoted on 5G and spectrum.

nodes.name: John Forte
nodes.description: President and CEO of Virginia Tech Applied Research Corporation (VT-ARC).

nodes.name: Charles "Chas" Richard
nodes.description: President of the Institute for Defense Analyses since 14 March 2026.

nodes.name: Chris Brady
nodes.description: President of General Dynamics Mission Systems.

nodes.name: Steve Bowsher
nodes.description: CEO of In-Q-Tel, the US intelligence community strategic investor.

nodes.name: Brian MacCarthy
nodes.description: Founder and Managing Partner of Booz Allen Ventures.

nodes.name: Steve Hopkins
nodes.description: President and CEO of ANSER since December 2019.

nodes.name: Evan Regan-Levine
nodes.description: Chief Strategy Officer of JBG SMITH. Manages its venture investments and led the National Landing CBRS spectrum and 5G smart city work.

nodes.name: Greg Simer
nodes.description: Chief Technology Officer of Northrop Grumman. Spoke for Northrop as a founding member of National IQ in February 2026.

nodes.name: Christopher T. Calio
nodes.description: Chairman and CEO of RTX. Vice Chair of the AIA Board of Governors for 2026.

nodes.name: Thomas A. Bell
nodes.description: CEO of Leidos since May 2023.

nodes.name: Daniel Ateya
nodes.description: Head of RTX Ventures since its founding in 2022.

nodes.name: Michael Manuccia
nodes.description: Inaugural CEO of National IQ, named September 2026.

nodes.name: Mike Keating
nodes.description: Executive Director of the Silicon Valley Defense Group.

nodes.name: Stephen Winchell
nodes.description: 24th Director of DARPA since May 2025.

nodes.name: Bill Collier
nodes.description: Co-lead of VC in DC. Also with Noblis Ventures.

nodes.name: Matt Gittleman
nodes.description: Co-founder and co-lead of VC in DC. Investment Director at JHH vc.

nodes.name: Mobile Satellite Services Association (MSSA)
nodes.description: Non-profit association founded in February 2024 by Viasat, Terrestar Solutions, Ligado Networks, Omnispace and Yahsat to integrate satellite and terrestrial networks on 3GPP NTN standards. Released Reference Architecture 2.0 (regenerative payloads; NR and NB-IoT on one constellation) in September 2026. Became a 3GPP Market Representation Partner on 22 October 2026.

nodes.name: European Space Agency (ESA)
nodes.description: Its Space for 5G/6G & Sustainable Connectivity program runs the 5G/6G Telecom Lab at ESTEC and co-runs NTN and direct-to-device innovation challenges with GSMA Foundry, with access to up to €100M announced at MWC26.

nodes.name: Global Certification Forum (GCF)
nodes.description: Device certification body with 300+ members. Has certified 3GPP NTN NB-IoT devices for GEO since 2024, with NGSO NB-IoT and NR-NTN expected in 2026. Signed an NTN certification MoU with MSSA on 24 September 2026.

nodes.name: 5G Automotive Association (5GAA)
nodes.description: Connected-vehicle association. Signed an MoU with MSSA in February 2025 on terrestrial and non-terrestrial network integration for vehicles, and runs an NTN work item on 3GPP-based automotive satellite connectivity.

nodes.name: SES
nodes.description: Multi-orbit GEO and MEO satellite operator. SES Techcom was a partner in the 6G-NTN project. In August 2026 SES expanded its investment and collaboration with Elveo Mobile for global direct-to-device services.

nodes.name: Telit Cinterion
nodes.description: IoT module and connectivity company. Telit Cinterion Deutschland was a partner in the SNS JU 6G-NTN project.

nodes.name: Martel Innovate
